| `message_id`                                     | Connects the run to the reply it produced. It must belong to `thread_id`.                                                        |
| `user_message_id`                                | Connects the run to the stored user message that started the turn, even when no reply was stored. It must belong to `thread_id`. |
| `model_id` and `provider`                        | Populate the model and provider dimensions.                                                                                      |
| Token counts, `duration_ms` and `first_token_ms` | Populate usage and timing when your backend measured them.                                                                       |
| `error`, `error_code` and `outcome_type`         | Describe an incomplete or failed run.                                                                                            |
| `trace_id`                                       | A 32 character lowercase hexadecimal trace id lets a client report merge with server spans.                                      |
| `environment`, `release` and `tags`              | Add deployment and filter dimensions.                                                                                            |

Storing the user message queues title generation; the report does not. The title is a later background write to the thread, so it is not in the message response either. See [Thread titles](/docs/cloud/thread-titles) and [Run reports](/docs/cloud/run-reports).

## Send the same calls from another language

The four requests above are plain HTTP. A Python, Go or Java service sends the same URL, JSON bodies and headers. `Content-Type: application/json` is required for JSON request bodies. The thread and message external ids make retries safe when the body and message role stay the same.

An `external_id` repeat with a different body updates that message and returns `200`. A repeat with a different `content.role` fails instead, which prevents a user message from becoming an assistant reply or the reverse.

This Python script performs the same sequence and carries the returned ids into each later request.

```
import os

import requests

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update(
    {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ASSISTANT_API_KEY']}",
        "Aui-User-Id": "user_123",
        "Aui-Workspace-Id": "workspace_acme",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
)
base_url = "https://backend.assistant-api.com"

thread_response = session.post(
    f"{base_url}/v1/threads",
    json={
        "last_message_at": "2026-09-17T09:30:00.000Z",
        "external_id": "slack-C0123-1758100200.000100",
        "upsert": True,
    },
    timeout=30,
)
thread_response.raise_for_status()
thread_id = thread_response.json()["thread_id"]

user_response = session.post(
    f"{base_url}/v1/threads/{thread_id}/messages",
    json={
        "parent_id": None,
        "external_id": "slack-1758100200.000100-user",
        "format": "ai-sdk/v6",
        "content": {
            "role": "user",
            "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "Where is my order?"}],
        },
    },
    timeout=30,
)
user_response.raise_for_status()
user_message_id = user_response.json()["message_id"]

assistant_response = session.post(
    f"{base_url}/v1/threads/{thread_id}/messages",
    json={
        "parent_id": user_message_id,
        "external_id": "slack-1758100200.000100-assistant",
        "format": "ai-sdk/v6",
        "content": {
            "role": "assistant",
            "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "Your order is on its way."}],
        },
    },
    timeout=30,
)
assistant_response.raise_for_status()
assistant_message_id = assistant_response.json()["message_id"]

run_response = session.post(
    f"{base_url}/v1/runs",
    json={
        "thread_id": thread_id,
        "status": "completed",
        "message_id": assistant_message_id,
        "user_message_id": user_message_id,
        "model_id": "gpt-6-luna",
        "provider": "openai",
        "input_tokens": 48,
        "output_tokens": 12,
        "duration_ms": 742,
    },
    timeout=30,
)
run_response.raise_for_status()
```

The same body shapes work from Go or Java.

## Export traces instead of reports

If your backend already emits OpenTelemetry, it can export traces without separately posting a run report. Send OTLP JSON or protobuf to `POST /v1/traces` with `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>` and an OTLP `Content-Type`. Trace export is API-key only; `Aui-Workspace-Id` is optional for that route and defaults to its trace workspace.

Each imported trace becomes a run. Set `gen_ai.conversation.id` to the Cloud thread id to link it to the conversation. A matching 32 character trace id also merges a later client report into the imported run. See [Traces](/docs/cloud/traces).

## Read a project

The project read API is API-key only and reads across every workspace in the project. Use it for operational views that do not belong to one end user.

| Need                       | Route                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Threads and their messages | `GET /v1/projects/threads` and `GET /v1/projects/threads/{thread_id}/messages` |
| Runs and one run's spans   | `GET /v1/projects/runs` and `GET /v1/projects/runs/{run_id}`                   |
| Usage                      | `GET /v1/projects/usage/daily` and `GET /v1/projects/usage/period`             |
| Scores                     | `GET /v1/projects/scores`                                                      |

```
curl "https://backend.assistant-api.com/v1/projects/threads?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ASSISTANT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Aui-User-Id: user_123" \
  -H "Aui-Workspace-Id: workspace_acme"
```

`POST /v1/mcp` offers read-only tools for runs, threads, scores, topics and usage. It also requires an API key and `Aui-Workspace-Id`. See [API](/docs/cloud/api) and [MCP](/docs/cloud/api/mcp).

## Troubleshooting

| What you see                                 | Why                                                                                         | What to do                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `403` when using an API key                  | The key was sent to a project frontend host instead of `https://backend.assistant-api.com`. | Send API-key traffic to the backend host.                                                                        |
| `403` with `Invalid Aui-Workspace-Id header` | A non-trace API-key request omitted the workspace header or supplied an invalid value.      | Send a nonempty workspace id with no whitespace or control characters.                                           |
| `402` with `plan_limit_reached`              | A new user message would exceed the active-user cap for the current usage period.           | Wait for the next period or change the project's plan. Repeats of an existing message do not trigger this check. |
| `409` with `Message role cannot change`      | An existing message `external_id` was repeated with a different `content.role`.             | Keep each external id bound to its original role. Use a new external id for another message.                     |
| A trace is not attached to its thread        | `gen_ai.conversation.id` did not equal a Cloud thread id in the project.                    | Set it to the `thread_id` returned by the create or upsert request.                                              |

# Stored message formats
URL: /docs/cloud/formats

The message formats Assistant Cloud stores, converts, and reads for thread titles.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Assistant Cloud stores a format name with every message. The format preserves the writer's message shape, while a message read can request a compatible AI SDK shape.

## The stored formats

| Format      | Writer                                                                    | Stored shape                                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aui/v0`    | The assistant-ui cloud history adapter and external-store runtime copies. | An assistant-ui thread message with `content`, attachments, status, and metadata. |
| `ai-sdk/v6` | The `aiSDKV6FormatAdapter`.                                               | An AI SDK UI message without its message `id`.                                    |
| `ai-sdk/v5` | Older AI SDK message writers.                                             | The older AI SDK message row, retained as a readable format.                      |

## The `aui/v0` shape

`aui/v0` is the complete assistant-ui message shape. It is stored with `format: "aui/v0"`.

### Message fields

| Field         | Required | Shape                                                             |
| ------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | No       | Local message ID. The encoder does not store it at the top level. |
| `createdAt`   | No       | ISO date string. The encoder does not store it at the top level.  |
| `role`        | Yes      | `assistant`, `user`, or `system`.                                 |
| `status`      | No       | The assistant-ui message status.                                  |
| `content`     | Yes      | Array of message parts.                                           |
| `attachments` | No       | Array of attachment wrappers.                                     |
| `metadata`    | Yes      | State, annotations, data, steps, and custom values.               |

### Message parts

| Type                                   | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`                                 | `text`, optional `id`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `reasoning`                            | `text`, optional `id`, `unstable_summary`, `timing`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `source` with `sourceType: "url"`      | `id`, `url`, optional `title`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `source` with `sourceType: "document"` | `id`, `title`, `mediaType`, optional `filename`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `tool-call`                            | `toolCallId`, `toolName`, one of `args` or `argsText`, and optional `result`, `artifact`, `modelContent`, `providerMetadata`, `isPreliminary`, `isError`, `interrupt`, `timing`, `mcp`, `approval`, `parentId`, nested `messages`, and `unstable_interactions`. |
| `image`                                | `image`, optional `id`, `filename`, and `providerMetadata`.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `file`                                 | `data`, `mimeType`, optional `id`, `filename`, `sourceType`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `data`                                 | `name`, `data`, optional `id`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `audio`                                | `audio: { data, format }`, where format is `mp3` or `wav`.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `generative-ui`                        | `spec`, optional `id` and `parentId`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

For text, reasoning, image, file, and data parts, the host-supplied `id` keys the part when it is non-empty and no other part of the same type in the message shares it, preserving component state when parts are reordered or updated with the same id. Every part with a missing or empty id, or an id shared by another part of the same type, is keyed by its type and position. The format preserves optional ids on attachment content parts too.

### Attachments and metadata

| Item                            | Fields                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Attachment wrapper              | `id`, `type`, `name`, optional `contentType`, `status`, and `content`.                           |
| Attachment `text`               | `text`, optional `id`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`.                                       |
| Attachment `image`              | `image`, optional `id`, `filename`, and `providerMetadata`.                                      |
| Attachment `file`               | `data`, `mimeType`, optional `id`, `filename`, `sourceType`, `providerMetadata`, and `parentId`. |
| Attachment `audio`              | `audio: { data, format }`, where format is `mp3` or `wav`.                                       |
| Attachment `data`               | `name`, `data`, optional `id`.                                                                   |
| `metadata.unstable_state`       | Optional JSON value.                                                                             |
| `metadata.unstable_annotations` | Array of JSON values.                                                                            |
| `metadata.unstable_data`        | Array of JSON values.                                                                            |
| `metadata.steps`                | Array whose entries may have `usage.inputTokens` and `usage.outputTokens`.                       |
| `metadata.custom`               | JSON object for application values.                                                              |

### Encode a message

The encoder drops the top level `id` and `createdAt`, because the server supplies those values. It rewrites a `running` status as `{ type: "incomplete", reason: "cancelled" }`.

Attachments are stored only on a `user` message and only when that message has attachments. A tool call stores `args` when `JSON.stringify(args)` equals `argsText`; otherwise it stores `argsText`. A tool result that cannot serialize as JSON is omitted, and one that loses data is stored as its JSON form. A non JSON `artifact` is dropped. A non JSON data value is written after a warning. Nested tool messages keep their own ID and ISO `createdAt`.

Runtimes that keep their transcript in their own backend, including LangGraph, LangChain, ADK, and custom external stores, copy eligible messages as `aui/v0`. Each copy has `parent_id: null`, uses the runtime message ID as `external_id`, and uses the preceding copied message ID as `parent_external_id`. Empty IDs and IDs longer than 255 characters are skipped.

AG-UI stores the final agent state in `metadata.unstable_state` and activity in data parts named `agui-activity/<type>`. AG-UI and A2A store A2UI surfaces as `present` tool calls whose `artifact.a2ui` carries the operations. A2A stores task artifacts in `metadata.custom.a2a.artifacts` without inline file bytes.

An unsupported message part throws `Message part type not supported by aui/v0: <type>`. An unsupported attachment part throws `Attachment part type not supported by aui/v0: <type>`.

### Decode a message

The decoder injects the server message ID and `created_at`, and exposes the stored `parent_id` as `parentId`. The history adapter decodes leniently. It drops unreadable parts and nested messages, then skips unreadable or orphaned rows. A nested tool message without an ID receives one synthesized from the containing message ID, tool call ID, and its indexes. A message with no status decodes as `{ type: "complete", reason: "unknown" }`.

## The `ai-sdk/v6` shape

`ai-sdk/v6` stores a UI message without its `id`. On read, the adapter adds the server message ID and the server parent ID as `parentId`.

Its telemetry reader examines assistant messages only. It opens a step for each `step-start` part, concatenates text parts into output text, and reads a tool's arguments from `input` or `args` and its result from `output` or `result`. A `tool-<name>` part is a frontend tool, while a `dynamic-tool` part with `toolName` is an MCP tool. Tool calls mark their step as `tool-calls`, and sampling calls are attached by tool call ID from `metadata.samplingCalls`. Tool artifacts, interactions, and approval responses use `metadata.__aui_toolArtifacts`, `metadata.__aui_toolInteractions`, and `metadata.__aui_toolApprovalResponses`.

Usage comes from `metadata.usage`, or from the sum of `metadata.steps[].usage` when that is absent. The reader sums usage across assistant messages and reads the model ID from message metadata. It reports `completed` when any text or tool call exists, and `incomplete` otherwise.

## The `ai-sdk/v5` shape

`ai-sdk/v5` is the older AI SDK row with `role` and `parts`. It remains readable and can be converted to `ai-sdk/v6`. Its tool parts carry `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `state`, `input`, optional `output`, and optional `errorText`.

When converted from `aui/v0`, a tool call has `output-error` when `isError` is true, `output-available` when `result` is present, and `input-available` otherwise. `isError` wins when both are present. Any `result` other than `undefined` counts as present, including `false`, `0`, an empty string and `null`. During a v5 to v6 conversion, `output-error` becomes an error result and tries to parse `errorText` as JSON.

During a server conversion from `aui/v0` to `ai-sdk/v5` or `ai-sdk/v6`, tool `artifact` and `unstable_interactions` move to the corresponding `__aui_toolArtifacts` and `__aui_toolInteractions` metadata keys. A v6 row spreads `metadata.custom` into its metadata. Data parts become `data-<name>` parts, and document sources become `source-document` parts. Generative UI becomes a `data-generative-ui` part, images and audio become `file` parts, and unknown parts become `data-<type>` parts.

## Read a compatible format

Pass `format` to `GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}/messages` or `GET /v1/projects/threads/{thread_id}/messages` to request a compatible row.

```
const { messages } = await cloud.threads.messages.list(
  "thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
  { format: "ai-sdk/v6" },
);
console.log(messages);
```

```
curl "https://backend.assistant-api.com/v1/threads/thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U/messages?format=ai-sdk%2Fv6" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ASSISTANT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Aui-User-Id: user_123" \
  -H "Aui-Workspace-Id: workspace_123"
```

| Requested format | Stored format     | Result                         |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `ai-sdk/v6`      | `aui/v0`          | Converted to `ai-sdk/v6`.      |
| `ai-sdk/v6`      | `ai-sdk/v5`       | Converted to `ai-sdk/v6`.      |
| `ai-sdk/v5`      | `aui/v0`          | Converted to `ai-sdk/v5`.      |
| Any other pair   | Any stored format | Returned in its stored format. |

If a stored row cannot be parsed or converted, the list skips that row and logs a warning. It does not fail the whole response.

## Extract text for a thread title

Thread title generation reads only messages whose `role` is `user` or `assistant`. A user message with no extracted text is omitted; an assistant message with no extracted text remains as an empty message. The title model then uses the first user and first assistant message, and only their text.

| Format      | Text source                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `aui/v0`    | `content` parts whose type is `text`, joined in order. |
| `ai-sdk/v5` | `parts` whose type is `text`, joined in order.         |
| `ai-sdk/v6` | `parts` whose type is `text`, joined in order.         |

# Limits
URL: /docs/cloud/limits

Every limit a project enforces, in one place.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Most limits protect a project from an accidental flood and apply across plans. The per project numbers at the end vary by plan.

## Rate limits

| What                                            | Limit        | Keyed by       |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------- |
| Creating an anonymous session                   | 30 a minute  | client address |
| Refreshing an anonymous session                 | 120 a minute | client address |
| Engagement event requests, each up to 50 events | 600 a minute | user           |

A limited request answers `429 { "error": "rate_limited" }` with a `Retry-After` header. Threads, messages, run reports, scores, traces, the project read API, and MCP are not rate limited.

## Request sizes

| Object                                                                 | Limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Thread title                                                           | 1 to 255 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Thread `external_id`                                                   | 1 to 255 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Thread `metadata`                                                      | 16 keys. Keys are at most 64 characters and values are at most 512 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Thread and message route IDs                                           | 1 to 255 characters. A message list cursor is at most 256 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Message `content`                                                      | At most 1,048,576 serialized characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Messages deleted per request                                           | 1 to 200 IDs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Run `thread_id`, `message_id`, `user_message_id`, and `trace_id`       | `thread_id` accepts 1 to 255 characters; each other ID accepts 1 to 48 characters. A trace ID is a W3C trace ID only when it matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Run `root_span_id`                                                     | Exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters, matching `^[0-9a-f]{16}$`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Run `error` and `error_code`                                           | 2,048 and 64 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Run `tags`                                                             | 20 tags of 64 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Run `environment` and `release`                                        | 64 and 255 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Run `attributes`, with `metadata` and unknown top level keys merged in | 16,384 serialized bytes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Run `steps`, `tool_calls` and `sampling_calls`                         | 1,000 entries each                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Run `output_text`, tool arguments, tool results, and step input        | 50,000 characters each                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Token counts                                                           | Whole numbers from 0 to 100,000,000                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Event batch                                                            | 1 to 50 events                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Event `props`                                                          | At most 1,024 UTF-16 code units in `JSON.stringify(props)` on the endpoint; `cloud.events.track` leaves `props` out when that JSON is over 1,024 bytes of UTF-8. Keys are 1 to 64 characters and string values are at most 256 characters.                                                                 |
| Event `value`                                                          | Whole number from 0 to 2,147,483,647                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Event IDs                                                              | `thread_id`, `message_id`, and `run_id` are each 1 to 48 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Score `name` and `comment`                                             | 1 to 64 and 1 to 2,000 characters. The name uses letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Score targets                                                          | `thread_id`, `message_id`, and `run_id` are each 1 to 48 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Score `string_value`                                                   | 1 to 255 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Attachment upload                                                      | Filename is 1 to 255 characters. Declared content length is at most 25 MiB.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Trace export body                                                      | At most 4,194,304 bytes, or 4 MB, after gzip or deflate decompression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Trace span count                                                       | At most 500 spans per trace.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Span attributes                                                        | 16,384 serialized bytes. Largest entries are dropped first when a trace is assembled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Allowed origins                                                        | 32 entries of 255 characters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Renderer URL                                                           | At most 2,048 characters after URL normalization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Aui-Sdk` header                                                       | The client accepts any printable name and version token. The server reads only the first 8 space separated tokens and records unique lowercase npm style names with strict SemVer versions, discarding duplicates. Each recorded name is at most 214 characters and each version is at most 64 characters. |
| API key user and workspace headers                                     | Each is 1 to 255 characters and cannot contain whitespace or control characters. `Aui-Workspace-Id` is required for every API key request except trace export. `Aui-User-Id` defaults to `__SYSTEM__`; trace export without a workspace ID uses `__OTLP__`.                                                |
| Auth rule fields                                                       | `name` and `provider` are 1 to 255 characters. `jwks_url`, `audience`, and `issuer` are 1 to 2,047 characters when present. `workspace_id_field` and `name_field` are at most 255 characters when present.                                                                                                 |
| Harness                                                                | Name is 1 to 80 characters. An ID matches `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`. A harness has at most 16 backend entries.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Assistant execution                                                    | `max_steps` defaults to 10 and accepts 1 to 50. `timeout_seconds` defaults to 300 seconds and accepts 30 to 600 seconds.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Thread title input                                                     | At most 8,000 characters across the first user and assistant text. When the assistant has text, it receives up to 500 characters before the user allocation is calculated.                                                                                                                                 |

A run report that exceeds validation caps is refused with `400`. A trace body larger than 4 MB is refused with `413`. The client trims telemetry tags before sending, but an oversized report received by the API is refused rather than trimmed.

# The assistant-cloud client
URL: /docs/cloud/sdk

Construct the Assistant Cloud client, choose authentication, and use its namespaces.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`assistant-cloud` is the JavaScript client for Assistant Cloud. It reaches a project frontend host with a JWT or anonymous session, or the backend host with an API key and user and workspace headers.

## Package and entry points

| Item                        | Value                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Package                     | `assistant-cloud`, the 0.2 line                                                                                                                            |
| Runtime dependency          | `assistant-stream`                                                                                                                                         |
| Optional peers              | `@opentelemetry/api`, `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http` and `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` for the telemetry entry, and `ai` for the AI SDK entry |
| `assistant-cloud`           | The client, persistence, reporting, events, scores, and sampling helpers.                                                                                  |
| `assistant-cloud/ai-sdk`    | AI SDK message storage and telemetry helpers.                                                                                                              |
| `assistant-cloud/telemetry` | OpenTelemetry trace exporter, span processor, and message metadata helpers.                                                                                |

## Construct the client

```
import { AssistantCloud } from "assistant-cloud";

const cloud = new AssistantCloud({
  baseUrl: "https://proj-<id>.assistant-api.com",
  authToken: async () => token,
});
```

`AssistantCloud` exposes `threads`, `projects`, `auth.tokens`, `auth.invalidate`, `runs`, `files`, `events`, `scores`, `telemetry`, and `registerSdk`. It has no `dispose` method. Call `cloud.events.dispose()` when an event buffer must flush and its listeners must be removed.

| Configuration arm | Fields                                                                        | Default     | Behaviour                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| JWT               | `baseUrl: string`, `authToken: () => Promise<string \| null>`                 | None        | Sends the callback result as a bearer token.                                       |
| API key           | `apiKey: string`, `userId: string`, `workspaceId: string`, `baseUrl?: string` | Backend URL | Sends an API key as a bearer token with `Aui-User-Id` and `Aui-Workspace-Id`.      |
| Anonymous         | `baseUrl: string`, `anonymous: true`                                          | None        | Creates and refreshes an anonymous session in browser storage.                     |
| Shared            | `telemetry?: boolean \| AssistantCloudTelemetryConfig`                        | Enabled     | Controls run reports, engagement events, and copies of external-store transcripts. |

The client chooses an arm in this order: `authToken`, then `apiKey`, then `anonymous`. Any other configuration throws `Invalid configuration: Must provide authToken, apiKey, or anonymous configuration`. Base URL normalization removes one trailing `/`.

### Configure telemetry

| Field          | Default                          | Effect                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`      | `true`                           | `false` prevents run reports, events, and copies of external-store transcripts. `true` and an omitted option are equivalent.                            |
| `events`       | `true` when telemetry is enabled | `false` keeps run reports and prevents engagement events.                                                                                               |
| `messages`     | `true` when telemetry is enabled | `false` keeps run reports and events but stops copies of external-store transcripts. Tool interactions then reject.                                     |
| `release`      | Omitted                          | Added to every run report.                                                                                                                              |
| `environment`  | Omitted                          | Added to every run report.                                                                                                                              |
| `tags`         | Omitted                          | Trimmed, limited to 64 characters, deduplicated, and limited to 20 entries. An empty result is omitted.                                                 |
| `beforeReport` | Omitted                          | Runs last, after environment, release, and tags are added. Returning `null` skips the send without consuming the report key. A thrown error is ignored. |

### Choose authentication

**JWT.** The client caches a token until it is within 30 seconds of its JWT expiry and shares one pending callback invocation. It sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A null or empty callback result makes the request throw `Authorization failed`. Recreate a runtime-backed client when the signed-in user or workspace changes so the runtime also drops the previous session's loaded data. For a client used outside a runtime, call `cloud.auth.invalidate()` before the next request; this clears the cached credential and pending engagement events. Every response is inspected for an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, which refreshes the cache only when it belongs to the request's current identity. A response authorization header with another scheme throws `Invalid auth header received`.

**API key.** The client does no token caching or network work. Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, `Aui-User-Id: <userId>`, and `Aui-Workspace-Id: <workspaceId>`.

**Anonymous.** The refresh record is stored in `localStorage` under `aui:refresh_token:<normalized base URL>`. The client migrates the old `aui:refresh_token` entry once. Storage failures and unavailable storage leave the session without persistence.

An anonymous client shares an in flight token request for the same storage and base URL, and uses the Web Lock `assistant-cloud:anonymous-auth:<base URL>` when Web Locks are available. A refresh token valid for more than 30 seconds is sent to `/v1/auth/tokens/refresh`. A `429` or server error throws `Assistant Cloud token refresh failed with status <status>`; another failed refresh falls through to `/v1/auth/tokens/anonymous`. A refresh token within 30 seconds of expiry is removed. Both requests have a 30,000 millisecond deadline and throw `Assistant Cloud <operation> timed out after 30000ms` if it expires. Invalid token response shapes throw `CloudResponseError`. `readAnonymousRefreshToken(baseUrl)` returns a stored token only when it remains valid for more than 30 seconds.

## Identify the SDK and send requests

`registerSdk({ name, version })` trims both strings and ignores the identity unless each is a nonempty run of printable ASCII characters with no spaces. It registers each `name/version` once, in first insertion order. Every request carries `Aui-Sdk`, beginning with `assistant-cloud/<version>` and followed by registered identities separated by spaces. The server reads only the first eight space-separated tokens and records unique entries only when their names use lowercase npm style names and their versions use strict SemVer.

The client adds `/v1` to every namespace route, serializes object bodies as JSON, and always sets `Content-Type: application/json`. The caller can set `Accept`, but cannot replace the content type or `Aui-Sdk`. Query strings use `URLSearchParams`: `true` becomes `true`, numbers become strings, and `false` is dropped. `threads.list` and `projects.threads.list` send `is_archived` as a string, so `is_archived: false` reaches the server. Only event delivery uses `keepalive`.

Most client requests have no retry policy. Scheduled and 20-event event flushes retry a failed send after 250 milliseconds and then 1,000 milliseconds. `CloudRunReporter` does not retry either, but it releases a report key after a `CloudAPIError` with status `429`, so a later observation can send that report. A `204`, `content-length: 0`, or blank response body resolves as `undefined`.

## Handle errors

`CloudAPIError` is thrown for every non successful HTTP response. It has `status`, optional `code`, and optional `details`. The response body supplies its message only from a nonempty `message` string; otherwise the message is `Request failed with status <status>, <body>`. A string `error` becomes `code`, and `details` becomes a shallow copy of the response object without `error`, including an empty object. A nonobject, array, or unparseable body supplies none of those fields.

`CloudResponseError` means a successful response did not have the shape a method expects. Its message is `Invalid Assistant Cloud response for "<field>": expected <expectation>`.

```
import { CloudAPIError, CloudResponseError } from "assistant-cloud";

async function findThread(threadId: string) {
  try {
    return await cloud.threads.get(threadId);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof CloudAPIError && error.status === 404) return null;
    if (error instanceof CloudAPIError) {
      console.error(error.status, error.code, error.details);
    }
    if (error instanceof CloudResponseError) console.error(error.message);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Use the client namespaces

Unless a row says otherwise, a data response can throw `CloudAPIError` for an HTTP failure and `CloudResponseError` for an invalid successful response.

### Threads and messages

| Method                            | Signature                                                                                                                                                                                                | Route                                                    | Errors           |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `cloud.threads.list`              | `(query?: { is_archived?: boolean; limit?: number; after?: string }) => Promise<{ threads: CloudThread[] }>`                                                                                             | `GET /threads`                                           | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.get`               | `(threadId: string) => Promise<CloudThread>`                                                                                                                                                             | `GET /threads/{threadId}`                                | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.create`            | `(body: { last_message_at: Date; title?: string; metadata?: unknown; external_id?: string; upsert?: boolean }) => Promise<{ thread_id: string }>`                                                        | `POST /threads`                                          | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.update`            | `(threadId: string, body: { title?: string; last_message_at?: Date; metadata?: unknown; is_archived?: boolean }) => Promise<void>`                                                                       | `PUT /threads/{threadId}`                                | `CloudAPIError`. |
| `cloud.threads.claim`             | `(body: { refresh_token: string }) => Promise<{ moved: number }>`                                                                                                                                        | `POST /threads/claim`                                    | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.delete`            | `(threadId: string) => Promise<void>`                                                                                                                                                                    | `DELETE /threads/{threadId}`                             | `CloudAPIError`. |
| `cloud.threads.messages.list`     | `(threadId: string, query?: { format?: string; limit?: number; after?: string }) => Promise<{ messages: CloudMessage[] }>`                                                                               | `GET /threads/{threadId}/messages`                       | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.messages.create`   | `(threadId: string, body: { parent_id: string \| null; format: "aui/v0" \| string; content: ReadonlyJSONObject; external_id?: string; parent_external_id?: string }) => Promise<{ message_id: string }>` | `POST /threads/{threadId}/messages`                      | Both.            |
| `cloud.threads.messages.update`   | `(threadId: string, messageId: string, body: { content: ReadonlyJSONObject }) => Promise<void>`                                                                                                          | `PUT /threads/{threadId}/messages/{messageId}`           | `CloudAPIError`. |
| `cloud.threads.messages.feedback` | `(threadId: string, messageId: string, body: { type: "positive" \| "negative"; comment?: string }) => Promise<{ feedback_id: string; type: "positive" \| "negative"; comment?: string \| null }>`        | `POST /threads/{threadId}/messages/{messageId}/feedback` | Both.            |

`CloudThread` has `id`, `project_id`, `workspace_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `title`, `last_message_at`, `is_archived`, `external_id`, and `metadata`. The client converts a null thread title to `""` and reads workspace and project IDs from the response. `CloudMessage` has `id`, `parent_id`, `height`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `format`, `content`, and `external_id`.

```
const { thread_id } = await cloud.threads.create({
  last_message_at: new Date(),
  external_id: "order-1042",
  upsert: true,
});
await cloud.threads.messages.create(thread_id, {
  parent_id: null,
  format: "aui/v0",
  content: { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "My order 1042 arrived damaged." }] },
});
const { messages } = await cloud.threads.messages.list(thread_id, { format: "ai-sdk/v6" });
console.log(messages);
```

### Runs

| Method              | Signature                                                                                                                      | Route               | Errors                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cloud.runs.stream` | `(body: { thread_id: string; assistant_id: "system/thread_title"; messages: readonly unknown[] }) => Promise<AssistantStream>` | `POST /runs/stream` | `CloudAPIError`; `CloudResponseError` for no body or a content type whose first token is not `text/plain`. |
| `cloud.runs.report` | `(body: AssistantCloudRunReport) => Promise<{ run_id: string }>`                                                               | `POST /runs`        | Both.                                                                                                      |

`stream` is for `system/thread_title`. It sends `Accept: text/plain` and decodes a plain text `AssistantStream`. A run report can include `message_id` for the stored assistant reply and `user_message_id` for the stored prompt. Each message must belong to the reported thread; `user_message_id` can be supplied without `message_id`.

```
await cloud.runs.report({
  thread_id: "thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
  status: "completed",
  model_id: "gpt-6-luna",
  provider: "openai",
  input_tokens: 128,
  output_tokens: 96,
  duration_ms: 1420,
});
```

### Files and scores

| Method                                     | Signature                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Route                                                     | Errors |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `cloud.files.generatePresignedUploadUrl`   | `(body: { filename: string }) => Promise<{ success: boolean; signedUrl: string; expiresAt: string; publicUrl: string; key?: string }>`                                                                                                               | `POST /files/attachments/generate-presigned-upload-url`   | Both.  |
| `cloud.files.generatePresignedDownloadUrl` | `(body: { key: string } \| { url: string }) => Promise<{ signedUrl: string; expiresAt: string; key: string }>`                                                                                                                                       | `POST /files/attachments/generate-presigned-download-url` | Both.  |
| `cloud.scores.create`                      | `(body: { name: string; data_type: "numeric" \| "categorical" \| "boolean"; value?: number \| boolean; string_value?: string; comment?: string; thread_id?: string; message_id?: string; run_id?: string }) => Promise<AssistantCloudScoreResponse>` | `POST /scores`                                            | Both.  |

An upload response exposes `key` only when the server sent it. A score response has `score_id`, `name`, `data_type`, `value`, and `string_value`.

```
async function uploadPhoto(file: File) {
  const upload = await cloud.files.generatePresignedUploadUrl({ filename: file.name });
  await fetch(upload.signedUrl, {
    method: "PUT",
    headers: { "Content-Type": file.type },
    body: file,
  });
  return cloud.files.generatePresignedDownloadUrl(
    upload.key ? { key: upload.key } : { url: upload.publicUrl },
  );
}

await cloud.scores.create({
  name: "resolution",
  data_type: "numeric",
  value: 1,
  run_id: "run_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
});
```

### Events, tokens, and project reads

| Method                                 | Signature                                                                                                                  | Route                                       | Errors                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cloud.events.track`                   | `(event: AssistantCloudEvent) => void`                                                                                     | `POST /events`                              | Never surfaces delivery failures.                           |
| `cloud.events.dispose`                 | `() => void`                                                                                                               | `POST /events` when buffered                | Never surfaces delivery failures.                           |
| `cloud.auth.tokens.create`             | `() => Promise<{ token: string }>`                                                                                         | `POST /auth/tokens`                         | Both.                                                       |
| `cloud.auth.invalidate`                | `() => void`                                                                                                               | None                                        | Clears cached authentication and pending engagement events. |
| `cloud.projects.threads.list`          | `(query?: { is_archived?: boolean; limit?: number; after?: string }) => Promise<{ threads: CloudThread[] }>`               | `GET /projects/threads`                     | Both.                                                       |
| `cloud.projects.threads.messages.list` | `(threadId: string, query?: { format?: string; limit?: number; after?: string }) => Promise<{ messages: CloudMessage[] }>` | `GET /projects/threads/{threadId}/messages` | Both.                                                       |

`track` does nothing when events are disabled. Otherwise it normalizes an event, flushes at 20 buffered events, and otherwise waits 2,000 milliseconds. Failed scheduled and 20-event flushes retry after 250 milliseconds and then 1,000 milliseconds. `pagehide`, a hidden document, and `dispose()` make one best-effort flush and end a pending retry. Each request contains at most 50 events and uses `keepalive`. Setting `cloud.telemetry.enabled` or `cloud.telemetry.events` to `false` at runtime drops buffered events and cancels pending retries. Empty or overlength IDs are dropped, and invalid or oversize props are dropped as a whole. The project namespace is read only.

```
cloud.events.track({
  kind: "message_copied",
  thread_id: "thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
  message_id: "msg_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
});
window.addEventListener("beforeunload", () => cloud.events.dispose());
```

```
const server = new AssistantCloud({
  apiKey: process.env.ASSISTANT_API_KEY!,
  userId: "user_123",
  workspaceId: "workspace_123",
});

const { token } = await server.auth.tokens.create();

const { threads } = await server.projects.threads.list({ limit: 10 });
for (const thread of threads) {
  const { messages } = await server.projects.threads.messages.list(thread.id, {
    format: "ai-sdk/v6",
  });
  console.log(thread.title, messages.length);
}
```

## Generate a thread title

`generateThreadTitle(cloud, { threadId, messages }): Promise<string | null>` sends `system/thread_title` through `cloud.runs.stream`, joins every text delta, trims the result, and writes a nonempty result through `cloud.threads.update`. On a thread that already has a title the stream carries that title and the helper writes it back unchanged. An empty stream returns `null` and does not write a title.

```
import { generateThreadTitle } from "assistant-cloud";

const title = await generateThreadTitle(cloud, {
  threadId: "thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "My order 1042 arrived damaged." }] },
    { role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "text", text: "I can help with a replacement." }] },
  ],
});
if (title === null) throw new Error("The cloud returned no title.");
```

## Use the building blocks

| Building block                                      | Purpose                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CloudMessagePersistence`                           | Persists message IDs, waits for parent writes, pages history, and keeps a local to remote ID map.                         |
| `createFormattedPersistence`                        | Adds format encoding and decoding to a persistence implementation, filters its format, and reverses loaded messages.      |
| `CloudRunReporter`                                  | Builds and deduplicates telemetry reports, swallowing delivery failures and releasing a key only after a `429`.           |
| `createRunReport`                                   | Maps runtime telemetry into the run report wire shape and normalizes timing, text, usage, tags, release, and environment. |
| `CloudEngagementReporter`                           | Resolves runtime IDs and records interaction events with the event namespace.                                             |
| `wrapSamplingHandler` and `createSamplingCollector` | Capture model, usage, and duration for MCP sampling calls without interrupting the sampling handler.                      |

Use these with a [custom thread list](/docs/cloud/custom-thread-list) when the built in thread list adapter is not the right source of thread identity or history.

```
import { CloudRunReporter } from "assistant-cloud";

const reporter = new CloudRunReporter(cloud);
await reporter.report({
  threadId: "thread_0qzof3jPoDwr7K3agyJN3D4U",
  status: "completed",
  modelId: "gpt-6-luna",
  provider: "openai",
  usage: { inputTokens: 128, outputTokens: 96 },
  durationMs: 1420,
});
```

## Import AI SDK helpers

| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AISDKStorageFormat`       | Type     | A UI message without its `id`.                                                                           |
| `aiSDKV6FormatAdapter`     | Value    | Encodes `ai-sdk/v6` storage by dropping the message ID and restores the server ID and parent ID on read. |
| `AISDKMessageLike`         | Type     | The minimal AI SDK message shape used by telemetry extraction.                                           |
| `extractAISDKRunTelemetry` | Function | Extracts assistant text, tools, usage, model, steps, and sampling calls from AI SDK messages.            |

| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

# Engagement events
URL: /docs/cloud/engagement

Record the actions users take around an answer, how events reach Assistant Cloud, and how the dashboard turns them into engagement signals.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Engagement events record what a user does around an answer, such as sending, editing, stopping, copying, or approving a tool. They contain interaction metadata rather than message text. Feedback comments are stored with their ratings, not as engagement events. The assistant-ui cloud runtime reports these events automatically, and the dashboard uses them to show engagement and satisfaction. For explicit message feedback and application scores, see [Feedback and scores](/docs/cloud/scores).

## How events are recorded

The runtime subscribes once per thread list to its composer, message, thread, and store events at the root scope, so a visited thread that stays mounted in the background adds no second listener and a run that ends after the user switched away is still recorded. Each event is attributed by the thread id it carries. An event for a thread the list does not know is dropped rather than sent without a thread. It reports these 16 kinds.

| Kind                  | Runtime trigger                                                                       | `value`                                                         | `props`                                    | Delivery rule                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `message_sent`        | `composer.send` when `payload.messageId` is absent.                                   | Milliseconds since the thread's previous run ended, when known. | `{ chars, attachments }`                   | This is the only event resolved with a remote thread wait, so it may create the cloud thread. |
| `message_edited`      | `composer.send` when `payload.messageId` is present.                                  | None.                                                           | `{ chars }`                                |                                                                                               |
| `suggestion_clicked`  | `composer.send` when `payload.suggestion` is truthy.                                  | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `attachment_added`    | `composer.attachmentAdd`.                                                             | None.                                                           | `{ type }` when the content type is known. |                                                                                               |
| `attachment_failed`   | `composer.attachmentAddError`.                                                        | None.                                                           | `{ type }` when the content type is known. |                                                                                               |
| `run_stopped`         | `composer.cancel` or `thread.cancelRun`.                                              | Milliseconds that the run had been running.                     | None.                                      | It is suppressed when the runtime has no recorded run start.                                  |
| `message_regenerated` | `message.reload`.                                                                     | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `branch_switched`     | `message.branchSwitched`.                                                             | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `message_copied`      | `message.copied`.                                                                     | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `tool_approved`       | `thread.toolApprovalAnswered` with `payload.approved === true`.                       | None.                                                           | `{ toolCallId, toolName }`                 | Emitted when the approval answer is given.                                                    |
| `tool_rejected`       | `thread.toolApprovalAnswered` with `payload.approved === false`.                      | None.                                                           | `{ toolCallId, toolName }`                 | Emitted when the approval answer is given.                                                    |
| `speech_started`      | `message.speak`.                                                                      | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `voice_started`       | `thread.voiceStarted`.                                                                | None.                                                           | None.                                      |                                                                                               |
| `error_shown`         | `message.error`.                                                                      | None.                                                           | `{ reason }`                               | Once per run. A new run start clears that run's error record.                                 |
| `suggestions_shown`   | A store watcher finds that the main thread is empty and has `suggestions.length > 0`. | The suggestion count.                                           | None.                                      | Once per thread.                                                                              |
| `thread_switched`     | `threads.selectionChanged`.                                                           | None.                                                           | None.                                      | Dropped when the selected thread has no remote id.                                            |

The runtime also remembers when each run starts and ends. That timing supplies the `message_sent` gap and the `run_stopped` duration. It keeps the remembered run endings, shown errors, and shown suggestions for up to 256 threads.

## Delivery, validation, and storage

`cloud.events.track` adds a normalized event to a local buffer and returns immediately. The client flushes as soon as 20 events are waiting, after a two second debounce, on the `pagehide` event, when document visibility becomes hidden, and when you call `dispose()`. A request carries at most 50 events and uses `keepalive: true`; `dispose()` removes the listeners, clears its timer, and flushes the buffer. Delivery never blocks the interface. A failed scheduled or 20-event flush retries after 250 milliseconds and then 1,000 milliseconds. A page-exit, hidden-page, or `dispose()` flush sends once and ends a pending retry.

Before buffering, the client applies these limits.

| Field                               | Normalization                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `run_id` | An empty id or an id longer than 48 characters is omitted.                                                                                                                       |
| `value`                             | Kept only when it is a nonnegative integer.                                                                                                                                      |
| `props`                             | Omitted as a whole when any value is not a string, finite number, or boolean; when a string is longer than 256 characters; or when the JSON encoding is larger than 1,024 bytes. |

The endpoint is `POST /v1/events` with `{ events }`. The server accepts 1 to 50 events, validates each `value` as an integer from 0 to 2,147,483,647, and accepts property keys of 1 to 64 characters. It silently drops an event that names a thread the caller does not own, while keeping the rest of the batch. A successful request answers `202` with `{ "accepted": n }`, where `n` is the number stored.

The event endpoint is limited to 600 requests per 60 seconds for each user. At the limit it answers `429`, `{ "error": "rate_limited" }`, and a `Retry-After` header.

The cloud keeps the raw event rows and a daily rollup by project, UTC day, user, and kind. The rollup records a count, a value sum, and a value count. It also keeps four thread flags from event kinds: `copied`, `stopped`, `regenerated`, and `edited`.

## What the dashboard derives

The dashboard's satisfaction value is a rule over the thread's ratings, flags, and run count, not a model judgement. A thumbs up on any message makes the positive side true, and a thumbs down on any message makes the negative side true. A rating outranks behaviour: positive behaviour counts only on a thread with no thumbs down, and negative behaviour only on a thread with no thumbs up. A thread with both ratings is mixed.

```
positive = threads.thumbs_up OR (NOT threads.thumbs_down AND (threads.copied OR threads.run_count >= 2))
negative = threads.thumbs_down OR (NOT threads.thumbs_up AND (threads.stopped OR threads.regenerated OR threads.edited))
satisfied    = positive AND NOT negative
mixed        = positive AND negative
dissatisfied = negative AND NOT positive
none         = NOT positive AND NOT negative
```

The signal filter on [Threads](/docs/cloud/dashboard/threads) uses these values.

| Signal        | Event or rule                                   | Label                 |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `stopped`     | `run_stopped`                                   | Stopped               |
| `regenerated` | `message_regenerated`                           | Regenerated           |
| `copied`      | `message_copied`                                | Copied                |
| `edited`      | `message_edited`                                | Edited and resent     |
| `attachment`  | `attachment_added`                              | Attached a file       |
| `suggestion`  | `suggestion_clicked`                            | Clicked a suggestion  |
| `branch`      | `branch_switched`                               | Switched branch       |
| `approved`    | `tool_approved`                                 | Approved a tool       |
| `rejected`    | `tool_rejected`                                 | Rejected a tool       |
| `error`       | `error_shown`                                   | Saw an error          |
| `no_reply`    | A named thread has no assistant message.        | No reply              |
| `loop`        | A thread has exact repeats or a rephrased turn. | Repeated or rephrased |

![Engagement on the demo project](/_next/static/immutable/media/engagement.3vl-famvjrf7z.webp)

### What the Engagement page shows

[Engagement](/docs/cloud/dashboard/engagement) answers what people do around responses. It opens with the **Answered**, **Continued**, **Stopped**, **Regenerated**, **Copied**, and **Came back** tiles, then shows the **Feedback** block. It then shows the conversation funnel, the satisfaction split, interaction mix, reactions and satisfaction over time, results by model and topic, and an hour by weekday heatmap. **Features used** groups attachment use, suggestion impressions and clicks, branching, tool approvals and rejections, read aloud, voice input, thread switching, errors shown, and attachment failures.

## From your code

Use `cloud.events.track` when your UI has an interaction that the runtime does not report. The call joins the next delivery batch.

```
cloud.events.track({
  kind: "suggestion_clicked",
  thread_id: threadId,
  props: { source: "sidebar" },
});
```

```
cloud.events.track({
  kind: "error_shown",
  thread_id: threadId,
  value: 1,
  props: { code: "upstream_timeout" },
});
```

After delivery, the event appears in the thread page's **Activity** tab and in the Engagement page's counts.

To keep run reports while turning off engagement events, set `events` to `false`. Set telemetry itself to `false` to turn off both run reports and events.

```
import { AssistantCloud } from "assistant-cloud";

const cloud = new AssistantCloud({
  baseUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL!,
  anonymous: true,
  telemetry: { events: false },
});
```

## Troubleshooting

| What you see                                     | Why                                                                                                            | What to do                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No new events                                    | Telemetry is off, or `telemetry.events` is `false`.                                                            | Enable telemetry, or remove the events override.                                                                                       |
| An interaction is absent from the dashboard      | The event named an unknown or unowned thread, so the server silently dropped it.                               | Send the cloud thread id for the current user.                                                                                         |
| The last interaction is missing after navigation | The flush made when the page hides or unloads was not delivered; it is sent once and never retried.            | Let the scheduled flush run before navigating away.                                                                                    |
| Satisfaction has no signal                       | The thread has no thumbs rating and none of the positive or negative behaviour facts in the satisfaction rule. | A thumbs up or a copy or second run supplies a positive fact; a thumbs down or a stop, regeneration, or edit supplies a negative fact. |
