| `checkboxes`                     | An array of selected values, empty when nothing is checked                                                       |
| `plain_text_input`               | The typed text                                                                                                   |
| `number_input`                   | The entered number                                                                                               |
| `button`                         | The raw `value` string, when it is not a serialized object                                                       |

A `{ "$field": name }` reference to a named `Checkbox` resolves from state values to `true` when checked or `false` when unchecked.

For the two halves of a local datetime, `$input` is the merged `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` value rather than the individual selection. A `{ "$field": name }` reference uses the same canonical value. Keep the picker's `block_id` on the action entry passed to the decoder so it can recover the temporal metadata.

### Reading a tree back

`fromSlackBlocks` is the inverse direction, mapping a Block Kit payload into vocabulary nodes and returning `{ nodes, warnings }`. It accepts a bare array or a `{ blocks }` wrapper.

The round trip is faithful on the plain building blocks (text, images, facts, controls, tables, simple cards) and documented-lossy elsewhere: context elements all return as `Caption`, so the `Badge` distinction is gone, a `CheckboxGroup` with a single option returns as a `Checkbox`, button styles beyond `primary` and `danger` are dropped, an alert's title and description come back merged into the description, and card layouts flatten to the fields the `card` block carries. Card footers are re-derived from button style, with the primary-styled button becoming `confirm`; when style cannot decide it, position does, and that emits a `fallback` warning. An input keeps its `action_id` as `$action` only when its block sets `dispatch_action` or the input is multiline, so a passive single-line input, including one from a form, returns without an action and stays passive when converted back.

Native `timepicker` and `datetimepicker` elements return as `DatePicker` nodes with `inputType: "time"` and `inputType: "datetime"`. A native datetime's initial Unix timestamp becomes a `Z` value at seconds precision. Reverse conversion reads each control separately, so a local datetime pair returns as separate date and time nodes.

## Before interactions work

Converting and posting a tree needs only a bot token with `chat:write`. Making its buttons do anything additionally needs, on the Slack app side:

- **Interactivity enabled with a request URL**, under Interactivity & Shortcuts. Slack posts every `block_actions` payload there.
- **An acknowledgement within 3 seconds.** Return HTTP 200 first and do the work afterwards; the payload's `response_url` accepts up to five follow-up posts within 30 minutes if you need to update or replace the message.
- **[Request signature verification](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/verifying-requests-from-slack)** on that endpoint, using your signing secret.

Receiving the webhook, verifying it, and routing the decoded action to your handler stay your application's responsibility. The converter only maps JSON to JSON.

## Reference

The generated per-export reference, including every type in the subpath, is at [Slack Block Kit](/docs/api-reference/generative-ui/slack). For the Teams equivalent of this page, see [Generative UI on Microsoft Teams](/docs/tools/generative-ui-teams).

# Moving to spec mode
URL: /docs/tools/generative-ui-spec-migration

Map a present tree, its actions, and its setup onto generative-frame spec mode, and keep present for what spec mode does not do.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`present` and [generative-frame's spec mode](/generative-frame/docs/spec-mode) render the same component vocabulary, so moving between them changes what the model writes, not what the user sees. A `present` call is one nested tree. A `render_spec` call is a flat spec of elements, streamed as JSON Patch lines, with state, bindings, conditions, repetition, and validation that the model gets back as feedback.

## When to move

Spec mode fits UI that holds state the model does not write: controls that feed each other, a list rendered from state with `repeat`, a section that shows only when `visible` holds, or a button that reads other controls' values. Its catalog checks every element, and `render_spec` returns the issues for the model to fix.

Keep `present`, alone or registered next to spec mode, for anything below, since spec mode has no equivalent:

- [A2UI](/docs/tools/a2ui) surfaces arrive as synthesized `present` calls, so an app that receives them needs `present` on the client.
- `promptUser()` waits for the user, sends the answer back as the tool result, and locks the answered controls. A spec handler's return value is discarded.
- `Text`, `Caption`, and `Markdown` grow as their props stream in. In spec mode each element appears whole once its patch line arrives.

For answers that need a widget or plain Markdown instead, see [Choosing an answer format](/docs/tools/generative-ui-formats).

## Setup

Build the catalog from the same library and add spec mode to a widget toolkit. Its tools run in the browser and upload their schemas, so the route from the [quick start](/docs/tools/generative-ui#quick-start) serves them through `frontend` without changes.

```
"use client";

import {
  createWidgetToolkit,
  useWidgetInstructions,
} from "generative-frame/assistant-ui";
import { createSpecToolkit } from "generative-frame/spec/assistant-ui";
import { defaultGenerativeUILibrary } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";
import { toSpecCatalog } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec";
import { approveOrder } from "@/lib/orders";

const { catalog, components } = toSpecCatalog(defaultGenerativeUILibrary, {
  actions: {
    approve_order: {
      description: "Approves the order in `orderId`.",
      params: {
        type: "object",
        properties: { orderId: { type: "string" } },
        required: ["orderId"],
      },
    },
  },
});

export const widgets = createWidgetToolkit({
  spec: createSpecToolkit(catalog, {
    components,
    handlers: {
      approve_order: (params) => approveOrder(String(params["orderId"])),
    },
  }),
});

export function WidgetInstructions() {
  useWidgetInstructions(widgets.tools);
  return null;
}
```

Register it in the provider from the quick start. Spread the two toolkits in that client module rather than in the `"use generative"` file, since the compiler cannot analyze a spread entry, and render `<WidgetInstructions />` inside the provider, which tells the model to load the `spec` module of `read_me` before it writes a spec:

```
"use client";

import {
  AssistantRuntimeProvider,
  AuiConfig,
  Tools,
} from "@assistant-ui/react";
import { useChatRuntime } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk";
import { lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls } from "ai";
import toolkit from "./toolkit";
import { WidgetInstructions, widgets } from "./widgets";

export function MyRuntimeProvider({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  const runtime = useChatRuntime({
    sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,
  });
  const config = AuiConfig({
    tools: Tools({ toolkit: { ...toolkit, ...widgets.toolkit } }),
  });

  return (
    <AssistantRuntimeProvider runtime={runtime} config={config}>
      <WidgetInstructions />
      {children}
    </AssistantRuntimeProvider>
  );
}
```

`useWidgetInstructions(widgets.tools, { preload: { modules: ["spec"] } })` puts that guidance in the system prompt instead, saving the model a call at the cost of a longer prompt.

`createWidgetToolkit` also registers the frame tools (`read_me`, `show_widget`, `edit_widget`, and `preview_widget`), so the model can answer with a sandboxed widget when the vocabulary cannot express something.

## The same card in both formats

As a `present` call:

```
{
  "_type": "Card",
  "title": "Order #1042",
  "children": [
    { "_type": "Fact", "label": "Total", "value": "$42.00" },
    {
      "_type": "Button",
      "label": "Approve",
      "_action": { "type": "approve_order", "orderId": "1042" }
    }
  ]
}
```

As the `patches` of a `render_spec` call titled `order_1042`, one operation per line:

```
{"op":"add","path":"/root","value":"order-card"}
{"op":"add","path":"/elements/order-card","value":{"type":"Card","props":{"title":"Order #1042"},"children":["order-total","approve"]}}
{"op":"add","path":"/elements/order-total","value":{"type":"Fact","props":{"label":"Total","value":"$42.00"}}}
{"op":"add","path":"/elements/approve","value":{"type":"Button","props":{"label":"Approve"},"on":{"press":{"action":"approve_order","params":{"orderId":"1042"}}}}}
```

## Mapping

| `present`                                                 | Spec mode                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A node's `_type`                                          | An element's `type`, stored under its id in `elements`                                                                                         |
| Props next to `_type`                                     | The element's `props`                                                                                                                          |
| Nested `children`, strings included                       | `children` as element ids; text needs its own `Text` element                                                                                   |
| `_key` on a list item                                     | The element id, or `repeat.key` for items rendered from state                                                                                  |
| `_action: { type, ...payload }`                           | An `on` binding for the component's event, such as `"on": { "press": { "action": "approve_order", "params": { "orderId": "1042" } } }`         |
| `createActionRegistry({ approve_order })`                 | `actions` in the `toSpecCatalog` options and `handlers` in `createSpecToolkit`                                                                 |
| A handler's `payload.$input`                              | `{ "$event": "" }` in the binding's `params`                                                                                                   |
| `{ "$field": "note" }` in an action                       | `{ "$bindState": "/note" }` on the control's value prop and `{ "$state": "/note" }` in the binding's `params`                                  |
| `streamProperties` and `$status: "streaming"`             | Elements appear whole as patch lines arrive; components always receive `$status: "done"`                                                       |
| `present()` renders inline unless `display: "standalone"` | `createWidgetToolkit` renders `render_spec`, `show_widget`, and `edit_widget` standalone unless `display: "inline"`                            |
| Props reach components unchecked                          | `render_spec` checks the spec against the catalog and returns the issues, and the renderer shows a placeholder for an element whose props fail |

[Spec mode](/docs/tools/generative-ui#spec-mode) lists the events each vocabulary component emits and what `$event` holds for each, and shows how your own components declare theirs.

## Slack and Teams

`specToUISpec(spec, { state })` from `@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec/tree` converts a spec into the `present` tree that the [Slack](/docs/tools/generative-ui-slack) and [Teams](/docs/tools/generative-ui-teams) converters and `generativeUIToJSX` take, as the spec looks for one state. `state` defaults to `spec.state`; pass a store's `getState()` to send what the user changed. Like the Slack and Teams subpaths, this one is React-free; it needs only `generative-frame`.

```
import { toSlackBlocks } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/slack";
import { specToUISpec } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec/tree";

const { blocks } = toSlackBlocks(specToUISpec(spec, { state }));
```

The conversion runs the mapping above backwards. Conditions, `repeat`, and expressions resolve against the state with generative-frame's [`resolveSpec`](/generative-frame/docs/spec-mode#resolve-to-a-static-tree). The binding on the first event a component emits, and on the event a `Card` footer button emits, becomes the node's `$action`: the first action in the binding other than `setState`, with its params resolved. A control whose value is bound gets a `name` unless it has one: its element id for `$bindState`, or its state path for `$bindItem`, which differs per item. Controls that would share a name, such as a control repeated per item with a static `name`, are named by their state paths instead. A param that reads a bound control's state, with `{ "$state": ... }` or with `{ "$item": ... }` inside a `repeat`, becomes a `{ "$field": ... }` reference to that control's `name`, with its value at conversion as the `fallback`, so the action reads what the user entered on the platform. A param that reads a path above bound controls, such as a whole form object or a list item, carries such a reference in each control's place. A param that reads `$event` is left out, because the platform passes what the event carries as `$input`: on Slack the value of the control that fired, and on Teams every other input on the card, keyed by id. `watch` and named slots have no equivalent and are left out.

# Generative UI on Microsoft Teams
URL: /docs/tools/generative-ui-teams

Convert a generative UI tree into an Adaptive Card, send it from a bot, and decode the Action.Submit payload Teams sends back into your action handlers.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

The generative UI tree your assistant renders in the browser is plain JSON, so it does not have to stay in the browser. `@assistant-ui/generative-ui/teams` converts the same tree into an [Adaptive Card](https://adaptivecards.io/explorer/) and decodes the submit payload a Teams bot receives back.

The subpath is React-free, so a server action, queue worker, or bot handler imports it without pulling React into the bundle.

## Sending a card

```
import { toAdaptiveCard } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/teams";

const { card, warnings } = toAdaptiveCard({
  $type: "Card",
  title: "Order #48213",
  children: [{ $type: "Text", value: "Shipped, arriving Thursday." }],
});

await context.sendActivity({
  attachments: [
    {
      contentType: "application/vnd.microsoft.card.adaptive",
      content: card,
    },
  ],
});
```

A spec from [spec mode](/generative-frame/docs/spec-mode) converts with `specToUISpec` from the React-free `@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec/tree` first, as [Moving to spec mode](/docs/tools/generative-ui-spec-migration#slack-and-teams) describes.

`toAdaptiveCard(node)` returns `{ card, warnings }` and never throws; an input it cannot convert comes back as an empty card plus one warning. `toTeamsAttachments(node)` wraps the same conversion in the [attachment envelope](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-reference) for you, which is the form you want for a carousel.

Cards are stamped at Adaptive Cards schema **1.5**, the version [Teams supports on desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-reference). Teams mobile clients cap at 1.2, so a card using 1.5-only elements (notably `Table`) may not render there.

## Warnings

Conversion is total. Every downgrade is reported rather than thrown:

```
type TeamsConversionWarning = {
  code: "clamped" | "dropped" | "fallback" | "advisory";
  component: string; // the IR component name, or "Root" for whole-payload issues
  detail: string;
};
```

`clamped` means content was truncated or capped, `dropped` means a node or one of its props was discarded and may have left a placeholder note behind (a `Chart` becomes an omission note), `fallback` means the node rendered through a different construct than requested (buttons past the sixth moved to secondary mode, a renamed input id), and `advisory` means nothing was changed at all and the result may still render poorly or be refused (a `Row` beyond three columns, a card or carousel over the byte budget).

## Component mapping

| Component          | Adaptive Card output                                                                                   | Fidelity                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Header`           | `TextBlock` with heading style                                                                         | `size` is ignored; the heading always emits `large`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Text`             | `TextBlock`                                                                                            | Six text sizes collapse to five rendered sizes, four weights to bold or not, and the five subtle color tokens to `isSubtle` while `emphasis` is dropped                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Markdown`         | `TextBlock`, passed through verbatim                                                                   | Teams renders [a markdown subset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-format); headings, tables, images, and blockquotes render literally                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Caption`, `Badge` | Small subtle `TextBlock`                                                                               | The two become identical output                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Image`            | `Image`                                                                                                | A numeric `size` is dropped with a warning; `round` is dropped silently                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Fact`             | `FactSet`                                                                                              | Consecutive facts merge into one set; `delta` appends as the browser's directional chip in parentheses                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Table`            | Native `Table` with the first row as headers                                                           | Column formats produce the same formatted text as the browser; sorting and alignment are browser-only; requires schema 1.5, so it will not render on Teams mobile; a column without a string label keeps its position with an empty header and warns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Card`             | `Container`, with the title as a leading heading                                                       | Footer buttons become an `ActionSet` beside the container, not inside it; a form card with its own `$action` and no `confirm` footer also gets a "Submit" action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Alert`            | `Container` with a semantic style (`accent`, `good`, `warning`, `attention`)                           | Title and description become two text blocks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Carousel`         | Multiple attachments through `toTeamsAttachments`                                                      | See [Carousels](#carousels); a non-card child that would have rendered is dropped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ListView`         | One `Container` per item, separated after the first                                                    | A non-item child that would have rendered is dropped with a warning, and never reserves an input id                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ListViewItem`     | `Container`, with a select action when it carries an action                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Tabs`             | A bolder `TextBlock` with each label, followed by that panel                                           | Adaptive Cards has no tabs, so every panel shows in order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Steps`            | A bolder `TextBlock` per step, numbered, with a subtle detail `TextBlock` under it                     | An entry without a title is dropped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Timeline`         | One `Container` per item with a small subtle time, a bolder title, and the detail                      | An entry without a title is dropped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Citation`         | `Container` with the source or the link's domain, the title, and a subtle snippet                      | An `http` or `https` `url` makes the title a markdown link; a link written inside the snippet or source stays plain text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Diagram`          | A `Container` with one monospace `TextBlock` per line of the Mermaid source, then a small subtle title | Teams cannot draw the diagram; a TextBlock breaks lines only in lists, so each line gets its own; a source over 3,000 characters or 200 lines is clamped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Map`              | One `Container` per place with the label linked to OpenStreetMap and the detail                        | Teams cannot draw a map, so `route` is dropped silently; a place without valid coordinates is dropped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Button`           | `Action.Submit` inside an `ActionSet`                                                                  | Consecutive buttons merge into one set; `buttonStyle` is dropped, since Teams [ignores action styling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-reference)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Select`           | `Input.ChoiceSet`, compact                                                                             | An option without a string value is dropped with a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `RadioGroup`       | `Input.ChoiceSet`, expanded                                                                            | An option without a string value is dropped with a warning; descriptions append to the choice title                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `CheckboxGroup`    | `Input.ChoiceSet`, expanded, with `isMultiSelect`                                                      | Its value is the checked values joined by commas, so a value that contains a comma cannot be told apart; descriptions append to the choice title                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Checkbox`         | `Input.Toggle`                                                                                         | Its value is the string `"true"` or `"false"`; the `switch` variant uses the same element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Slider`           | `Input.Number`                                                                                         | `min`, `max`, `defaultValue`, and `label` map directly; submitted values are numbers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Input`            | `Input.Text`                                                                                           | Password uses `style: "password"`; number stays text and submits a string without native numeric validation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DatePicker`       | `Input.Date`, `Input.Time`, or both                                                                    | Date mode keeps `YYYY-MM-DD` values and bounds. Time mode uses `HH:mm`; nonzero seconds or fractions in the value or maximum are dropped with a `dropped` warning. Datetime mode pairs a date and time input; instants display in their own offset, shown in the label as `UTC` or `UTC±HH:mm`, because the card does not know the viewer's time zone. The date input accepts date-only bounds directly or takes the date part of datetime bounds; the time input has none. Nonzero seconds or fractions in wall clock datetime values are dropped with a `dropped` warning. An unsupported `inputType` renders as a date input with a `dropped` warning. |
| `Form`             | Children inline, then a "Submit" `ActionSet`                                                           | Adaptive Cards has no form container; inputs on the card submit together                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Row`              | `ColumnSet` with one auto-width column per child                                                       | Beyond three columns you get a warning, but all columns are kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Col`, `Box`       | `Container`                                                                                            | The two become indistinguishable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Divider`          | Nothing; sets `separator` on the next sibling                                                          | See [Layout differences](#layout-differences)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Spacer`           | Nothing; sets `spacing` on the next sibling                                                            | See [Layout differences](#layout-differences)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Chart`            | Replaced by a subtle note                                                                              | Always warns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Icon`             | Dropped                                                                                                | Silently                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

`Text`'s size collapse is narrower than it looks: `sm`, `lg`, `xl`, `2xl`, and `3xl` map to `small`, `medium`, `large`, `extraLarge`, and `extraLarge`, while `md` emits no `size` at all and renders at the card's default. So six tokens reach five rendered sizes, and only `2xl` and `3xl` become indistinguishable. Color splits rather than collapses: `secondary`, `alpha-70`, `white`, `white-70`, and `white-50` all set `isSubtle: true`, while `emphasis` maps to nothing the converter emits and is dropped outright, so emphasized text renders identically to unstyled text.

Teams has no undo surface, so a Button with `undoable` fires immediately.

Presentation props the converter does not map are dropped silently, without a warning, because the node itself still renders. That covers `Box`'s `width`, `height`, `radius`, and `background`; `Card`'s `padding` and `background`; `gap` on `Row`, `Col`, and `Form`, `align` on `Row` and `Col`, and `justify` on `Row`; `Badge`'s `variant`; `Carousel`'s `label`; `CheckboxGroup`'s `progress`; `Divider`'s `flush`; and `Button`'s `block`. `Button`'s `submit` is dropped for a different reason: every input on an Adaptive Card submits together, so a submit button and a click button both convert to the same `Action.Submit`.

On a `Card` marked `asForm`, the confirm action carries the `confirm` footer's `$action`, or the Card's own `$action` when the footer has none. A form card with its own `$action` and no `confirm` footer gets a "Submit" action where the confirm action would go, ahead of any cancel action.

## Layout differences

Two vocabulary components behave differently here than anywhere else, because Adaptive Cards models separation as a property of an element rather than as an element:

- A `Divider` emits nothing and sets `separator: true` on the next element that does emit.
- A `Spacer` emits nothing and sets `spacing: "large"` on the next element that does emit.

A component that emits nothing, such as an `Icon`, does not consume a pending mark; it carries through to the next real element. A `Divider` or `Spacer` with nothing after it disappears entirely, without a warning. As a result, a trailing separator you would see on Slack is absent on Teams.

Two consolidations also apply, both run-based rather than global: consecutive `Fact` siblings merge into one `FactSet`, and consecutive `Button` siblings merge into one `ActionSet`. A different component between them breaks the run and starts a new set.

## Inputs

Adaptive Cards merges every input's current value into one submit object keyed by the input's `id`, which has two consequences.

**Ids come from `name`.** Each control's `id` is its `name` prop, falling back to a per-type default (`"select"`, `"radiogroup"`, `"checkboxgroup"`, `"slider"`, `"input"`, `"datepicker"`). `Checkbox` is the exception: it falls back to its `label` first and only then to `"checkbox"`, so an unnamed checkbox keys the submit object by its visible label. Two controls that share a name on the same card would collide, so the converter renames the later one and warns. The key `aui` is reserved for the action envelope; a control named `aui` is renamed too. The `aui:datetime:` namespace is reserved for generated datetime inputs. A field name starting with that prefix is escaped with a leading `_` and a warning; `$field` references use the same mapping.

Datetime pickers use `aui:datetime:date:<encodeURIComponent(fieldId)>` for the date input and `aui:datetime:time:<encodeURIComponent(fieldId)>:<encodeURIComponent(previousValue)>` for the time input. Each ID identifies the field and its role on its own. The time ID's last segment holds the original instant, including its offset and precision, or is empty for a wall clock or initially empty value. Submit actions carry no temporal field map, so adding companion actions does not duplicate that metadata. Keep these IDs intact when forwarding input values to `decodeSubmitData`.

**There is no change event.** Adaptive Cards has no way to dispatch when a control's value changes, so a standalone control carrying `$action` gets a companion "Submit" `ActionSet` appended, plus a `fallback` warning. Five such controls produce five separate submit buttons. The idiomatic shape is to put `$action` on a `Form`, a `Card` marked `asForm`, or a `Card` footer and leave the controls actionless, which yields one submit for the whole card.

## Actions

### Outbound

A node's `$action` is carried inside the submit payload's reserved `aui` key, so it never collides with input values:

```
{
  "type": "Action.Submit",
  "title": "Approve",
  "data": { "aui": { "type": "approve_order", "payload": { "orderId": "48213" } } }
}
```

Unlike Slack, the payload is not serialized to a string and carries no size cap of its own, so the converter never drops or truncates it the way an oversized Slack button value is dropped. Size is checked once, against the whole card, and that check only warns; whether an oversized card is then accepted is decided by Teams.

### Inbound

A bot receives the merged submit object as `activity.value`. `decodeSubmitData` splits it back into the action your tree dispatched, with the card's input values under `$input`:

```
import { decodeSubmitData } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/teams";

const action = decodeSubmitData(context.activity.value);
// { type: "approve_order", orderId: "48213", $input: { quantity: "2" } }
```

`$input` here is an **object keyed by input id**, which differs from Slack, where a single control's `$input` is a bare value. It is omitted when no inputs were submitted. A datetime picker appears under its field ID in `$input`: the decoder combines its date and time inputs into `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`. If the picker started with an instant, the decoded value keeps its original offset spelling and precision. If only one half is submitted, or either half is `""`, the field value is `""`. A newly selected value from an empty picker has no offset because Teams supplies no viewer time zone. A `{ "$field": name }` reference in the payload resolves to this canonical field value, or to its `fallback` when neither half was submitted. The function returns `undefined` for a payload without a well-formed `aui` envelope, malformed temporal IDs or values, conflicting metadata for one field, or temporal IDs targeting an ordinary submitted field, and never throws; `type` always comes from the envelope, and a `$input` key smuggled into the payload is stripped.

The converter emits `Action.Submit`. Teams also offers [`Action.Execute`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/adaptive-cards/authoring-cards/universal-action-model) from schema 1.4, which lets a bot return a replacement card in the invoke response; reaching for that means constructing the action yourself.

## Carousels

A carousel is an activity-level construct on Teams rather than a card-level one, so it only works through `toTeamsAttachments`:

```
const { attachments, attachmentLayout } = toTeamsAttachments(tree);

await context.sendActivity({ attachments, attachmentLayout });
```

With a `Carousel` at the root you get one attachment per card child and `attachmentLayout: "carousel"`, capped at ten cards. Anywhere other than the root, a carousel falls back to its cards rendered in sequence, with a `fallback` warning. Input ids are scoped per card, so two attachments may safely reuse the same name.

## Limits

| Budget               | Value                                                              | Behavior when exceeded                                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Carousel attachments | 10                                                                 | Truncated                                               |
| Table                | 100 rows, 20 columns                                               | Truncated                                               |
| Choice options       | 100                                                                | Truncated                                               |
| Primary actions      | 6                                                                  | Later actions move to secondary mode; none are dropped  |
| Payload size         | 80,000 serialized bytes, set below Teams' 100 KB bot message limit | Warned, never truncated, so you decide whether to split |

Traversal is bounded as well: 200 children per level, 5,000 nodes per call, and 32 levels of element nesting, each reported as a `Root` warning. These bounds exist because the tree arrives from a model.

## Reference

The generated per-export reference, including every type in the subpath, is at [Microsoft Teams](/docs/api-reference/generative-ui/teams). For the Slack equivalent of this page, see [Generative UI on Slack](/docs/tools/generative-ui-slack).

# Generative UI
URL: /docs/tools/generative-ui

Let the model compose an interface at runtime from a component vocabulary you ship, using the present tool from @assistant-ui/generative-ui.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

With generative UI, you ship a **vocabulary** of components and let the model assemble them, instead of writing one component per tool. The model calls a single `present` tool whose arguments are a JSON tree of component names and props, and assistant-ui renders that tree.

The package ships a default vocabulary of 35 components (cards, facts, tables, charts, tabs, steps, timelines, citations, diagrams, maps, forms, controls), so the shortest useful setup registers one tool and writes no components at all.

## Which generative UI pattern?

assistant-ui uses "generative UI" for more than one thing. Two questions separate them: does the **model** compose the layout or do you bind it ahead of time, and does the UI originate from a **tool call** or from a part your backend emits. Pick the row that matches what you are building:

| Pattern                                                            | API                                         | Best for                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **The `present` tool** (this page)                                 | `JSONGenerativeUI` + `present`              | The model composes dashboards, cards, and layouts from a vocabulary you ship |
| **[Tool UI](/docs/tools/tool-ui)**                                 | toolkit `render`                            | A widget tied to a tool you already know about (forms, pickers, charts)      |
| **[Generative UI primitive](/docs/tools/generative-ui-primitive)** | `MessagePrimitive.GenerativeUI` + allowlist | A backend that already emits `generative-ui` message parts                   |
| **[LangGraph data UI](/docs/runtimes/langgraph/generative-ui)**    | `makeAssistantDataUI` + `ui_message`        | LangGraph agents emitting UI on the LangGraph stream                         |

The first two are tool-driven, so the model decides when UI appears; the last two are backend-driven, so your agent does. The backend-driven pair splits on transport rather than on either axis: the primitive reads a `generative-ui` message part, while LangGraph data UI reads `push_ui_message` off the LangGraph stream. `present` and the primitive both take a JSON component tree, but in [non-interchangeable shapes](/docs/tools/generative-ui-primitive#spec-shape). A third-party option also exists in the tool-driven space: [OpenUI](/docs/tools/openui) publishes an integration that streams OpenUI Lang through the same shape.

To decide between Markdown, `present`, spec mode, and a model-written widget for an answer, see [Choosing an answer format](/docs/tools/generative-ui-formats).

Browse every component the default vocabulary offers in the [component vocabulary reference](/elements/vocabulary), and see finished compositions in the [Generative section of Elements](/elements).

## Quick start

1. ### Install the package

   ```bash
   npm install @assistant-ui/generative-ui zod
   ```

   The vocabulary renders as unstyled semantic HTML with `data-aui` attributes. Add the styled library to get the shipped look:

   With the style-aware registry configured in components.json ("@assistant-ui": "https\://r.assistant-ui.com/styles/{style}/{name}.json"), the flavor resolves from the project style automatically:

   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest add @assistant-ui/generative-ui
   ```

   Or add by direct URL without registry configuration:

   ```bash
   npx shadcn@latest add https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/generative-ui.json
   ```

   Or install manually:

   ```bash
   npm install @assistant-ui/generative-ui@^0.0.8 react-markdown remark-gfm zod beautiful-mermaid leaflet tw-shimmer@^0.4.14
   ```

   Then copy these files (packaged registry content; the source links show where each ships from):

   - [components/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx](https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/generative-ui/components/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx) ([source](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx))
   - [components/assistant-ui/elements/mermaid-diagram.tsx](https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-mermaid-diagram/components/assistant-ui/elements/mermaid-diagram.tsx) ([source](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/elements/mermaid-diagram.tsx))
   - [components/assistant-ui/elements/geo-map.tsx](https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-geo-map/components/assistant-ui/elements/geo-map.tsx) ([source](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/elements/geo-map.tsx))
   - [components/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces.tsx](https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-surfaces/components/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces.tsx) ([source](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces.tsx))
   - [components/assistant-ui/utils/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.ts](https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-surfaces/components/assistant-ui/utils/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.ts) ([source](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/utils/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.ts))

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL --create-dirs \
     -o 'components/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx' https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/generative-ui/components/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx \
     -o 'components/assistant-ui/elements/mermaid-diagram.tsx' https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-mermaid-diagram/components/assistant-ui/elements/mermaid-diagram.tsx \
     -o 'components/assistant-ui/elements/geo-map.tsx' https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-geo-map/components/assistant-ui/elements/geo-map.tsx \
     -o 'components/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces.tsx' https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-surfaces/components/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces.tsx \
     -o 'components/assistant-ui/utils/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.ts' https://r.assistant-ui.com/base/files/elements-surfaces/components/assistant-ui/utils/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect.ts
   ```

   This merges the vocabulary stylesheet and theme variables into your CSS, which is what the rest of this page assumes, and lands `components/assistant-ui/elements/generative-ui.tsx`. That file exports `styledGenerativeUILibrary`, which differs from the default vocabulary in three entries: a real markdown renderer, and a drawn `Diagram` and `Map` (see [Diagrams and maps](#diagrams-and-maps)); [Styling](#styling) wires it in.

2. ### Enable the compiler

   The `"use generative"` directive lets one file declare tools that both the browser and your server route can import: the compiler strips the browser-only halves out of the server build and the schemas out of the client build.

   ```
   import { withAui } from "@assistant-ui/next";

   export default withAui({
     /* your Next config */
   });
   ```

   Vite and TanStack Start use `aui()` from `@assistant-ui/vite`; Expo and bare React Native use `withAui` from `@assistant-ui/metro`.

3. ### Expose the vocabulary as a tool

   `JSONGenerativeUI` turns a component library into the model-facing schema for `present`. Register the result on a toolkit like any other tool.

   ```
   "use generative";

   import { defineToolkit } from "@assistant-ui/react";
   import {
     JSONGenerativeUI,
     defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
   } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";

   const generative = new JSONGenerativeUI({
     library: defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
   });

   export default defineToolkit({
     present: generative.present({ display: "standalone" }),
   });
   ```

   `display: "standalone"` renders the result on its own surface, outside the chain-of-thought trace. Omit it to render inline.

4. ### Register the toolkit on the client

   ```
   "use client";

   import {
     AssistantRuntimeProvider,
     AuiConfig,
     Tools,
   } from "@assistant-ui/react";
   import { useChatRuntime } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk";
   import { lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls } from "ai";
   import toolkit from "./toolkit";

   export function MyRuntimeProvider({
     children,
   }: {
     children: React.ReactNode;
   }) {
     const runtime = useChatRuntime({
       sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,
     });
     const config = AuiConfig({ tools: Tools({ toolkit }) });

     return (
       <AssistantRuntimeProvider runtime={runtime} config={config}>
         {children}
       </AssistantRuntimeProvider>
     );
   }
   ```

   > [!warn]
   >
   > `present` is a frontend tool: it resolves in the browser, and the run only continues once its result is sent back. Without `sendAutomaticallyWhen`, the UI renders and the conversation then stops.

5. ### Serve the schema

   The route imports the same toolkit module. The compiler resolves that import to the server build, so only the schemas cross over and no browser code enters your server bundle.

   ```
   import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
   import { AISDKToolkit } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk";
   import { convertToModelMessages, stepCountIs, streamText } from "ai";
   import toolkit from "@/app/toolkit";

   const aiToolkit = new AISDKToolkit({ toolkit });

   export async function POST(req: Request) {
     const { messages, tools } = await req.json();

     const aiSDKTools = await aiToolkit.tools({ frontend: tools });

     const result = streamText({
       abortSignal: req.signal,
       model: openai("gpt-6-luna"),
       messages: await convertToModelMessages(messages, { tools: aiSDKTools }),
       stopWhen: stepCountIs(10),
       tools: aiSDKTools,
     });

     return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
   }
   ```

   `stopWhen` matters here for the same reason `sendAutomaticallyWhen` does: rendering the UI is one step, and the model needs another to say anything after it.

Ask for something the vocabulary can express, for example "show me a sales dashboard for the last six months", and the model will answer with a rendered composition. The complete setup runs in [`examples/with-generative-ui`](https://github.com/assistant-ui/assistant-ui/tree/main/examples/with-generative-ui).

## What the model emits

Every node is a flat object: `_type` names the component, `children` nests, and every other key is a prop.

```
{
  "_type": "Card",
  "title": "Q3 revenue",
  "children": [
    {
      "_type": "Row",
      "children": [
        { "_type": "Fact", "label": "Bookings", "value": "$1.2M" },
        { "_type": "Fact", "label": "Growth", "value": "+18%" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "_type": "Chart",
      "variant": "bar",
      "showAxis": true,
      "data": [
        { "label": "Jul", "value": 22 },
        { "label": "Aug", "value": 26 },
        { "label": "Sep", "value": 31 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`_type`, `_key`, and `_action` are reserved by the framework, as is every key beginning with `$` (such as the injected `$status`), and `children` follows the JSX convention. The model writes the reserved keys with `_` because Anthropic rejects tool schemas with `$` in property names; trees built in code, such as converter output and the `UIElement` type, write them as `$type`, `$key`, and `$action`, and both spellings render the same. Every other key is yours, so a component is free to declare props named `type`, `status`, or `variant` without colliding.

## Extending the vocabulary

`defineGenerativeComponents` adds your own components. Each one declares a zod schema for its props, a description the model reads, and a render function.

```
"use generative";

import { z } from "zod";
import {
  JSONGenerativeUI,
  defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  defineGenerativeComponents,
} from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";
import { WeatherCard } from "@/components/weather-card";

const generative = new JSONGenerativeUI({
  library: {
    ...defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
    ...defineGenerativeComponents({
      Weather: {
        description: "Show a weather card for a `get_weather` result.",
        properties: z.object({
          id: z.string().describe("The `id` returned by `get_weather`."),
        }),
        render: (props) => <WeatherCard {...props} />,
      },
    }),
  },
});
```

Set `streamProperties: true` alongside `properties` to receive partially-filled props while the model is still writing them. `render` then sees `Partial<P>` and an injected `$status` of `"streaming"`, and the full props once it turns `"done"`. Components opt out by default and render only once their props are complete.

> [!warn]
>
> Inside a `"use generative"` module, a `"use client"` module may be referenced **only** as the `render` value of an inline `defineGenerativeComponents` literal. The compiler drops `render` and the imports only it uses from the server build; referencing such a module from `properties`, `description`, a spread, or a top-level constant leaks a client reference into the server graph and breaks schema generation. `defaultGenerativeUILibrary` is safe on both builds.

## Actions

Pass an action registry to let rendered nodes call back into your app. The model puts an `_action` object on a node, and its `type` is matched against your handlers.

```
import {
  JSONGenerativeUI,
  createActionRegistry,
  defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
} from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";

const actions = createActionRegistry({
  purchase: async ({ payload }) => {
    await checkout(payload);
  },
});

const generative = new JSONGenerativeUI({
  library: defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  actions,
});
```

```
{
  "_type": "Button",
  "label": "Buy",
  "_action": { "type": "purchase", "sku": "pro-plan" }
}
```

### Undo window

Set `undoable` for sends and other hard-to-reverse actions. The button waits five seconds, shows Undo with a countdown, and another click or Escape cancels it.

```
{
  "_type": "Button",
  "label": "Delete order",
  "undoable": true,
  "_action": { "type": "delete_order", "orderId": "48213" }
}
```

`Select`, `Input`, `DatePicker`, `Checkbox`, `Slider`, `RadioGroup`, and `CheckboxGroup` add the user's value as `$input` when they fire the action; `Slider` sends a number and a `CheckboxGroup` sends the array of its checked option values. `Form`, and a `Card` with `asForm` set, add an object keyed by each control's `name` instead. On a `Card` the collected object is dispatched through `confirm._action`, or through the card's own `_action` when `confirm` has none, while `cancel._action` always fires without `$input`. Unknown action types are ignored and warn in development.

`Slider` takes `min`, `max`, an optional `step`, `defaultValue`, and `unit`; it shows the live value and commits only when the adjustment finishes. Set `Checkbox` `variant` to `"switch"` for a switch presentation without changing its boolean value. `RadioGroup` and `CheckboxGroup` options can add a short `description`, rendered under the label.

Any value inside `_action` can be a `{ "$field": name }` reference instead, which resolves to a control's current value when the action fires. It reads the control with that `name` in the nearest enclosing `Form` or `Card` with `asForm`, or else anywhere in the same `JSONGenerativeUI` render, collected the way a `Form` collects it. When no control holds a value, a reference written as `{ "$field": name, "fallback": value }` resolves to its `fallback`, and one without a fallback is dropped. A component outside the default vocabulary that dispatches `$action` itself reads no control, so each reference in it resolves the same way. Such a component can resolve references against its own values before it dispatches: `resolveFieldReferences(action, fields)` from `@assistant-ui/generative-ui` replaces each reference with the matching value in `fields`, falling back the same way, and `hasFieldReference(action)` tells whether an action carries any. A tree rendered with `renderGenerativeUI` directly resolves references only inside one of those forms or an element marked `data-aui="root"`, so they never read a host page's own form. `Input` and `Select` take a `defaultValue`, so a button can send an edited value without a form:

```
{
  "_type": "Col",
  "children": [
    {
      "_type": "Input",
      "name": "note",
      "label": "Delivery note",
      "defaultValue": "Leave at the door"
    },
    {
      "_type": "Button",
      "label": "Save",
      "_action": { "type": "save_note", "note": { "$field": "note" } }
    }
  ]
}
```

On Teams, `decodeSubmitData` resolves these references from the card's inputs. On Slack, pass the interaction payload's `state.values` alongside its action to `decodeBlockAction` to resolve references from named controls; a missing field uses its fallback when provided.

`Input` accepts an optional `inputType` of `"text"`, `"password"`, or `"number"` for a single line control, defaulting to text. A number input uses `step="any"` and keeps its value as a string, including decimal values such as `"12.5"` and `""` when cleared. Setting `multiline` renders a textarea instead.

`DatePicker` accepts `inputType` `"date"` (the default), `"time"`, or `"datetime"`. Its own `_action` runs once per committed value: a pick from the native picker commits at once, and a typed value commits on blur or on Enter outside a form. Date values use `YYYY-MM-DD`; time values use `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`; datetime values use `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` with optional seconds, fractional seconds, and an offset (`Z` or `±HH:mm`). A datetime with an offset displays in the viewer's time zone and submits with the same offset; one without an offset submits unchanged. The [A2UI converter](/docs/tools/a2ui#component-mapping) maps `DateTimeInput` to the matching type, and uses a text `Input` when its value cannot fit that type. A single choice A2UI `ChoicePicker` maps to `RadioGroup` even for a `chips` display hint, preserving an empty selection as `[]` and a selected value as a one item string array; `multipleSelection` maps to `CheckboxGroup`.

A control resets to its initial value (`defaultValue`, `defaultChecked`, or a `DatePicker`'s `value`) whenever a re-render changes that value, and otherwise keeps what the user entered.

Each `renderGenerativeUI` or `JSONGenerativeUI` render scopes native radio names, so separate cards can reuse a logical `name` without clearing each other's selection. Inside the same render and form scope, radio groups with the same logical name share one selection. The logical name remains the key for form values and `$field` references. If you mount multiple independent React apps on the same page, configure distinct [`identifierPrefix` values](https://react.dev/reference/react/useId#using-the-same-id-prefix-on-the-client-and-the-server) and use each app's same prefix for server rendering and hydration.

Each dispatched action, including its `$input`, is recorded on the tool call on a best-effort basis. Recording depends on the runtime and the interaction log's limits, and it never delays or prevents dispatch. When the UI is registered through `promptUser()`, a handler's non-`undefined` return value becomes the `prompt_user` tool result only when that call has no result yet. Whether the run then continues depends on the runtime, including how it treats human tools. `present` actions never create a tool result.

Once answered, a `prompt_user` locks its controls and shows the submitted values. Only values submitted through a `Form` or a `Card` with `asForm` are restored after a reload.

Without a registry, the tree still renders and model-emitted actions degrade to a no-op.

## Spec mode

In [generative-frame's spec mode](/generative-frame/docs/spec-mode), the model builds the UI as a flat spec, streamed as JSON Patch lines, with state, bindings, and validation. `toSpecCatalog` from `@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec` turns a library into the catalog and components spec mode takes, so the default vocabulary, or a styled library, renders there too. [Moving to spec mode](/docs/tools/generative-ui-spec-migration) maps a `present` setup onto it. Install `generative-frame` alongside it:

```
import { createWidgetToolkit } from "generative-frame/assistant-ui";
import { createSpecToolkit } from "generative-frame/spec/assistant-ui";
import { defaultGenerativeUILibrary } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";
import { toSpecCatalog } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec";

const { catalog, components } = toSpecCatalog(defaultGenerativeUILibrary, {
  actions: { purchase: { description: "Buys the plan in `sku`." } },
});

const widgets = createWidgetToolkit({
  spec: createSpecToolkit(catalog, {
    components,
    handlers: { purchase: (params) => checkout(params) },
  }),
});
```

A spec element binds behavior with `on` instead of carrying `_action`. A `Button` and a `ListViewItem` emit `press`, the value controls emit `change` (an `Input` emits `submit`), a `Form` emits `submit`, and a `Card` emits `cancel` from its cancel button and `confirm` from its confirm button or, with `asForm`, whenever it submits. The payload, which `{ "$event": "" }` reads, is the control's value, or every named control's value when a `Form` emits `submit` or a `Card` with `asForm` emits `confirm`. A control whose value prop (`defaultValue`, `defaultChecked`, or a `DatePicker`'s `value`) is bound with `$bindState` follows that state and writes every change back to it, inside a `Form` too. Declare host actions through `actions` so the model can bind them; `setState` is always available.

Your own components take part through the same library entry. Declare the `events` a component emits and the `slots` it renders: `$dispatch({ type, $input })` emits a declared event, the element's `$action` carries the first one when the element binds it, `default` slot content arrives as `children` and any other slot in `$slots`, and `slots: []` takes no children. A prop the spec binds with `$bindState` arrives as its current value, and `$bindings` holds a setter that writes a new one back to state. The `present` tool ignores `events` and `slots`, and present mode passes neither `$slots` nor `$bindings`. Declaring either on a vocabulary component replaces its spec events, slots, and description, so give the override its own `description` too, since the vocabulary's description covers `present` behavior.

```
import {
  defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  type GenerativeUIComponent,
} from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/react";
import { toSpecCatalog } from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Stars } from "@/components/stars";

const Rating: GenerativeUIComponent<{ value: number }> = {
  description: "A 1 to 5 star rating the user can change.",
  properties: z.object({ value: z.number().describe("Stars, from 1 to 5.") }),
  events: ["rate"],
  slots: [],
  render: ({ value, $bindings, $dispatch }) => (
    <Stars
      value={value}
      onChange={(stars) => {
        $bindings?.value?.(stars);
        $dispatch?.({ type: "rate", $input: stars });
      }}
    />
  ),
};

const { catalog, components } = toSpecCatalog({
  ...defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  Rating,
});
```

### With Vue

`@assistant-ui/generative-ui/vue` ships the vocabulary as Vue components for `SpecRenderer` from `generative-frame/spec/vue`, with `vue` as an optional peer. Its `toSpecCatalog` takes a Vue library and the same `actions` option, and every component renders the same `data-aui` markup, emits the same events with the same payloads, and writes bound values back the same way as the React vocabulary, so the stylesheet and the behavior above carry over:

```
import { defineComponent, h } from "vue";
import { SpecRenderer } from "generative-frame/spec/vue";
import {
  defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  toSpecCatalog,
  type GenerativeUIComponent,
} from "@assistant-ui/generative-ui/vue";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Stars } from "@/components/stars";

const Rating: GenerativeUIComponent = {
  description: "A 1 to 5 star rating the user can change.",
  properties: z.object({ value: z.number().describe("Stars, from 1 to 5.") }),
  events: ["rate"],
  slots: [],
  component: defineComponent({
    props: ["value"],
    emits: ["rate", "update:value"],
    setup(props, { emit }) {
      return () =>
        h(Stars, {
          value: props.value,
          onChange: (stars: number) => {
            emit("update:value", stars);
            emit("rate", stars);
          },
        });
    },
  }),
};

const { catalog, components } = toSpecCatalog({
  ...defaultGenerativeUILibrary,
  Rating,
});
```

A Vue entry carries a `component` instead of a `render` function. The component follows the [Vue component contract](/generative-frame/docs/spec-mode#render-with-vue): it declares its props and the events it emits, receives children and named slots as Vue slots, and writes a bound prop by emitting `update:<prop>`. To render `render_spec` calls in an `@assistant-ui/vue` thread, pass the catalog and components to `createSpecToolkit` from `generative-frame/spec/assistant-ui/vue` ([assistant-ui on Vue](/generative-frame/docs/assistant-ui#on-vue)).

### With React Native

On React Native, `@assistant-ui/generative-ui/spec` resolves to a React Native build through the `react-native` export condition: `toSpecCatalog` and `defaultGenerativeUILibrary` from it draw the same vocabulary with React Native's own components, with the same events, payloads, and bound values. [Generative UI on React Native](/docs/react-native/generative-ui) shows the setup and the components that take a different form on a phone.

## Charts

`Chart` accepts positive and negative values. Its scale always includes zero, so bars grow upward or downward from the zero line, areas fill to that line, and stacked bars and areas keep positive and negative totals on their respective sides. A chart that contains both positive and negative values draws a zero baseline. When `showAxis` is set, the ticks include zero and use round values for a mixed domain.

Bars and data points in line and area charts expose a native tooltip with the point label and formatted value. A point without a label shows its position, counting from 1. Tooltips on named series also include the series label. Sparklines remain compact and do not add point targets.

Use `series[].color` to set an individual series to `emphasis`, `secondary`, `alpha-70`, `white`, `white-70`, or `white-50`. The same color fills that series' legend swatch, while the legend label stays muted.

## Tables and facts
