The family is inherited through `var(--dg-font, inherit)`. There is no per-role size prop and no font prop.

## A fluid box

When the width comes from layout rather than from your code, `Fit` from `diagrammatic/interactive` measures its box and hands the width down. It renders `initial` (640 by default) on the server and on the first client render, then redraws at the measured width in steps of `step` pixels.

```
"use client";

import { Area } from "diagrammatic";
import { Fit } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

<Fit>{({ width }) => <Area data={signups} width={width} aspect={3} yTicks={3} />}</Fit>;
```

\[interactive preview omitted]

The chart inside the callback is a client component, because the callback is. Measure once at the wrapper; the charts never measure themselves.

## Text that does not fit

Nothing is drawn outside the box. A row label longer than its gutter is cut with an ellipsis, a legend that would cross the edge cuts its names, and an end value is pulled inside the frame. Widths are estimated as `chars × fontSize × 0.6`, because a server render cannot measure glyphs. `truncate`, `textWidth`, and `charsThatFit` are exported for laying out your own labels by the same rule.

# Small multiples
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/small-multiples

Lay any form out as a grid of panels on one shared scale.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`SmallMultiples` lays any form out as a grid of panels. Give every panel the same domain (here `yMax`) so the panels compare. Panel titles are your markup.

```
import { Line, SmallMultiples } from "diagrammatic";

<SmallMultiples columns={2} title="Active seats by region">
  {regions.map((region) => (
    <div key={region.name}>
      <p>{region.name}</p>
      <Line data={region.data} yMax={52} width={300} aspect={2} />
    </div>
  ))}
</SmallMultiples>;
```

# Theming
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/theming

The chart tokens, the shadcn/ui bridge, custom skins, and dark mode.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Every color a chart draws resolves through a `--dg-*` custom property, with the shipped value as its `var()` fallback. A chart renders correctly with no stylesheet at all, and reskins globally when you set the tokens. There is no color prop.

| Token                   | Role                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--dg-c1` to `--dg-c7`  | Categorical series, in a fixed order                                   |
| `--dg-pos` / `--dg-neg` | The diverging pair, gains and losses                                   |
| `--dg-ink`              | Single-series marks and text; `currentColor` by default                |
| `--dg-muted`            | Secondary text                                                         |
| `--dg-grid`             | Axes and grid lines                                                    |
| `--dg-surface`          | Separator strokes and occluding fills; set it to the card's background |
| `--dg-font`             | Chart text; inherits the host font by default                          |

## The shipped palette

The seven categorical hues are a validated set: each pair clears lightness, chroma, color-vision-deficiency separation, and contrast checks in both light and dark mode. Past seven categories, rank them and fold the tail into one `Other`, which is the honest chart anyway. A single-series chart draws in ink, not in a hue.

## shadcn/ui

Import the bridge next to the defaults:

```
@import "diagrammatic/styles.css";
@import "diagrammatic/shadcn.css";
```

It maps `--dg-c1` to `--dg-c5` onto `--chart-1` to `--chart-5` (the sixth and seventh fall back to the shipped hues), ink onto `--foreground`, muted onto `--muted-foreground`, grid onto `--border`, and surface onto `--background`. It reads each token as a complete color, the format shadcn/ui generates for Tailwind CSS v4. A Tailwind CSS v3 theme stores bare HSL channels, so wrap them yourself on the same selectors:

```
[data-dg],
[data-dg-legend] {
  --dg-c1: hsl(var(--chart-1));
  --dg-c2: hsl(var(--chart-2));
  --dg-c3: hsl(var(--chart-3));
  --dg-c4: hsl(var(--chart-4));
  --dg-c5: hsl(var(--chart-5));
  --dg-ink: hsl(var(--foreground));
  --dg-muted: hsl(var(--muted-foreground));
  --dg-grid: hsl(var(--border));
  --dg-surface: hsl(var(--background));
}
```

## Any other design system

Set the tokens you want on any ancestor, or on `[data-dg]` to reach every chart:

```
[data-dg],
[data-dg-legend] {
  --dg-c1: var(--brand-1);
  --dg-grid: var(--line);
  --dg-font: var(--font-mono);
}
```

## Dark mode

Ink, muted, and grid derive from `currentColor`, so they follow your text color into dark mode with no extra rule. The categorical hues are constant across modes, which is what lets white text sit on a series fill in both. Set `--dg-surface` to the background a chart sits on, so the separators between pie slices and treemap tiles match it.

## Marks are styleable

Every drawn mark carries `data-part="mark"` plus its address (`data-i`, `data-series`), and the other parts carry `data-part="grid"`, `"axis"`, `"legend"`, or `"region"`. Bars are plain `rect` elements with square corners, so you can round or restyle them from CSS:

```
svg[data-dg] [data-part="mark"]:is(rect) {
  rx: 3px;
}
svg[data-dg] [data-part="mark"]:hover {
  opacity: 0.8;
}
```

# Introduction
URL: /diagrammatic/docs

Seventy chart forms for React, drawn as server-rendered SVG with zero dependencies and themed by CSS tokens.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`diagrammatic` draws charts as SVG on the server. Every form is a pure function with no hooks and no browser APIs, so it renders in a React Server Component, in SSR, or in a static export as is. A figure is drawn in CSS pixels at a stated `width` and inherits the page's font, and its colors resolve through `--dg-*` custom properties, so it reskins with your design system and needs no configuration.

## Install

```bash
npm install diagrammatic
```

React 18 or 19 is the only peer. The package has no runtime dependencies.

## Draw a chart

```
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="Weekly active users"
      labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6"]}
      data={[1200, 1350, 1310, 1580, 1720, 1910]}
      yTicks={4}
    />
  );
}
```

No `"use client"`, no provider, and no stylesheet is required. Defaults are the product: a validated categorical palette, diverging pairs with a neutral midpoint, zero-based bars, and a legend whenever a chart has two or more named series.

## Entry points

| Entry                      | Contents                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `diagrammatic`             | 68 chart components, `SmallMultiples`, `Legend`, tile sets, and the scale and text helpers    |
| `diagrammatic/interactive` | `Root`, `Tooltip`, `Zoom`, `Fit`, `getMarkDatum`, `getSeriesColor`, `applyHighlight` (client) |
| `diagrammatic/spec`        | `Chart`, `validateSpec`, `CHART_TYPES`, and the `ChartSpec` type                              |
| `diagrammatic/world`       | `WorldMap` and `DotWorldMap` with their country geometry                                      |
| `diagrammatic/styles.css`  | Token defaults and the highlight styles                                                       |
| `diagrammatic/shadcn.css`  | A bridge from shadcn/ui theme tokens to chart tokens                                          |

# Quickstart
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/quickstart

Install diagrammatic, draw a chart in a Server Component, theme it, and add a tooltip.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

1. ### Install

   ```bash
   npm install diagrammatic
   ```

2. ### Draw a chart

   Import a form and pass it data. The component is a pure function, so it can live in a Server Component.

   ```
   import { StackedArea } from "diagrammatic";

   const series = [
     { name: "search", data: [42, 48, 51, 58, 61, 66, 64, 71, 77, 82] },
     { name: "direct", data: [30, 29, 33, 35, 34, 38, 41, 40, 43, 45] },
     { name: "referral", data: [12, 15, 14, 18, 22, 21, 25, 29, 28, 33] },
     { name: "social", data: [8, 9, 13, 12, 11, 15, 14, 18, 21, 19] },
   ];

   export default function Page() {
     return (
       <StackedArea
         title="Weekly sessions by channel"
         labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6", "W7", "W8", "W9", "W10"]}
         series={series}
         yTicks={4}
         format={(v) => `${v}k`}
       />
     );
   }
   ```

3. ### Match your theme

   Charts read their colors from `--dg-*` tokens with the shipped palette as the fallback, so this step is optional. A shadcn/ui app imports the bridge once and every chart takes its `--chart-*`, foreground, border, and background tokens:

   ```
   @import "diagrammatic/styles.css";
   @import "diagrammatic/shadcn.css";
   ```

   `styles.css` also carries the highlight styles that `Root` uses. See [Theming](/diagrammatic/docs/theming) for every token.

4. ### Add a tooltip

   Interaction lives in `diagrammatic/interactive`, a client entry that wraps the chart. The tooltip receives the address of the hovered mark, and you look the row up in data you already have.

   ```
   "use client";

   import { Bar } from "diagrammatic";
   import { Root, Tooltip } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

   export function BenchmarkChart({ items }: { items: { label: string; value: number }[] }) {
     return (
       <Root>
         <Bar title="Benchmark score" items={items} format={(v) => v.toFixed(1)} />
         <Tooltip side="top">
           {({ datum }) => {
             const item = items[datum.index ?? -1];
             return item ? <div className="tooltip">{item.label} {item.value}</div> : null;
           }}
         </Tooltip>
       </Root>
     );
   }
   ```

# Accessibility
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/accessibility

How a chart names itself to assistive technology, and where the numbers go.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

A chart is an image to a screen reader. `title` names it: the root `svg` gets `role="img"`, an `aria-label`, and an SVG `<title>`. `summary` adds a sentence in the figure's `<desc>`, which assistive technology reads after the title. A chart without a name is marked decorative with `aria-hidden`.

```
<Column
  title="Weekly deploys"
  summary="Deploys rose from 14 in week 1 to 31 in week 7, passing the goal of 25 in week 5."
  items={deploys}
  target={{ at: 25, label: "goal" }}
/>
```

Marks are pointer affordances and are not focus stops. When the numbers matter, render them in a table beside the figure, which is the accessible path and often the better reading for everyone:

- title

  Weekly deploys

- summary

  Deploys rose from 14 in week 1 to 31 in week 7, passing the goal of 25 in week 5.

- items

  - - label

      W1

    - value

      14

  - - label

      W2

    - value

      19

  - - label

      W3

    - value

      11

  - - label

      W4

    - value

      23

  - - label

      W5

    - value

      27

  - - label

      W6

    - value

      21

  - - label

      W7

    - value

      31

- target

  - at

    25

  - label

    goal

Show the data

| Week | Deploys |
| ---- | ------- |
| W1   | 14      |
| W2   | 19      |
| W3   | 11      |
| W4   | 23      |
| W5   | 27      |
| W6   | 21      |
| W7   | 31      |

fig. 01 · The figure and its table, from the same rows

## Color

The categorical palette clears color-vision-deficiency separation checks, and charts with two or more series draw a legend, so color is never the only key. Diverging forms pair a hue with a direction (left and right of zero), not hue alone.

## Motion

Charts are still by default. Flow trails and live-point pulses animate only when the chart or an ancestor carries `data-dg-motion` and `diagrammatic/styles.css` is loaded, and every motion rule sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a reader who asks for reduced motion sees the still figure. The highlight fade is the only other transition; see [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

# Charts from a model
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/ai-specs

Let a model emit a chart as JSON, validate it, and draw it with one component, in an assistant-ui thread or anywhere else.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`diagrammatic/spec` describes every form in the main entry as a serializable spec: the form's `type` plus its data props. A model can write that JSON, `validateSpec` checks it, and `Chart` draws it.

\[interactive preview omitted]

## The spec

```
{
  "v": "dg/1",
  "type": "column",
  "title": "Weekly deploys",
  "unit": "none",
  "items": [
    { "label": "W1", "value": 14 },
    { "label": "W2", "value": 19 }
  ]
}
```

| Field                                  | Description                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`                                 | The form, in kebab case: `"line"`, `"stacked-bar"`, `"sankey"`. `CHART_TYPES` lists all 68                        |
| `v`                                    | The spec shape version, `"dg/1"`. Optional; any other value fails validation                                      |
| `unit`                                 | How printed numbers are formatted: `"percent"`, `"compact"`, or `"none"`. A spec cannot carry a `format` function |
| `title`, `width`, `height`, `fontSize` | The chart's name and its pixel contract                                                                           |
| everything else                        | The form's data props, exactly as the component takes them                                                        |

Event handlers, `style`, refs, and `format` stay out, because a spec is JSON. `diagrammatic/world` is not part of the spec.

## Validate and draw

```
import { Chart, validateSpec } from "diagrammatic/spec";

const spec = validateSpec(JSON.parse(modelOutput));
<Chart spec={spec} />;
```

`validateSpec` checks that the type exists and that the form's required fields are present with the right shape, and throws an error naming the field when they are not. That message is written to be handed back to the model. A spec with an unknown type renders an inert placeholder instead of throwing, so a half-written stream cannot take the page down. `validateSpec` checks structure only; deep field checks stay with TypeScript through the `ChartSpec` type, so a malformed value inside a valid shape (an item that is not an object, say) can still throw while the chart renders. Render untrusted specs inside an error boundary.

## In an assistant-ui thread

Register a tool whose arguments are a spec. The tool runs in the browser, returns the validation error to the model when there is one, and renders the chart in the thread.

```
"use generative";

import { defineToolkit } from "@assistant-ui/react";
import { CHART_TYPES, Chart, validateSpec } from "diagrammatic/spec";
import { z } from "zod";

export default defineToolkit({
  render_chart: {
    description: `Draw a chart from data. "type" is one of: ${CHART_TYPES.join(", ")}.`,
    parameters: z.object({
      spec: z.looseObject({ type: z.string() }),
    }),
    execute: async ({ spec }) => {
      "use client";
      try {
        validateSpec(spec);
        return { drawn: true };
      } catch (error) {
        return { error: (error as Error).message };
      }
    },
    render: ({ args, status }) => {
      if (status.type === "running") return <div className="h-64 animate-pulse" />;
      try {
        return <Chart spec={validateSpec(args.spec)} />;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    },
  },
});
```

The tool result carries the validation error back, so the model's next step can repair the spec.

# Migrating from Recharts
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/migrating-from-recharts

Map a Recharts dashboard onto diagrammatic forms, sizing, axes, tooltips, color, and legends.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

A working map from a Recharts dashboard to `diagrammatic`, written from the parts that actually differ.

Two differences drive everything else. A recharts chart is a client component that measures its container and renders in pixel space; a diagrammatic chart is a server component that renders in pixel space at a stated `width`, so size is a host decision rather than a measurement and only a fluid box needs the client. And a recharts tooltip receives the row; a diagrammatic tooltip receives an address into the data the host already has.

## Forms

| recharts                               | diagrammatic                                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AreaChart` with one `Area`            | `Area data`                                                            |
| `AreaChart` with several `Area`        | `Area series`                                                          |
| `AreaChart` with `stackId`             | `StackedArea`                                                          |
| `LineChart`                            | `Line data` or `Line series`                                           |
| `BarChart`                             | `Column`, or `Bar` for a ranked horizontal breakdown                   |
| `BarChart layout="vertical"`           | `Bar`                                                                  |
| `BarChart` with `stackId`              | `StackedBar`, plus `normalize` for percent                             |
| several `Bar` side by side             | `GroupedBar`                                                           |
| `PieChart` with `innerRadius`          | `Pie inner center centerLabel`, plus `legend={false}` for a DOM legend |
| `Treemap`                              | `Treemap root`                                                         |
| `ScatterChart` with `ZAxis`            | `Scatter points[].size`                                                |
| `Scatter` with a `Cell` per category   | `Scatter points[].series`                                              |
| `RadarChart`                           | `Radar`                                                                |
| `FunnelChart`                          | `Funnel`                                                               |
| a hand-rolled hour by weekday grid     | `Heatmap mark="dot"`                                                   |
| a hand-rolled contribution calendar    | `Heatmap mark="calendar"`                                              |
| a hand-rolled composition bar          | `SplitBar items block`                                                 |
| a hand-rolled label truncation         | nothing: labels are cut to their margin                                |
| `ResponsiveContainer`                  | `width` and `height`, or `Fit` when the width is fluid                 |
| `CartesianGrid` plus `YAxis tickCount` | `yTicks={4}`                                                           |
| `XAxis ticks={...}`                    | `labels`, one per tick you want printed                                |
| `XAxis tick={{ fontSize: 12 }}`        | `fontSize={12}` on the chart, every role follows                       |
| `Tooltip content`                      | `Root` plus `Tooltip`, looking the row up by `datum.index`             |
| `Legend`                               | automatic, or `legend={false}` plus the DOM `Legend`                   |
| `isAnimationActive={false}`            | nothing to turn off                                                    |

## Sizing

```
<ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height={180}>
  <AreaChart data={rows}>…</AreaChart>
</ResponsiveContainer>
```

becomes, when the card width is known:

```
<Area data={values} labels={ticks} width={420} height={180} yTicks={4} />
```

and when it is not:

```
<Fit>
  {({ width }) => (
    <Area data={values} labels={ticks} width={width} height={180} yTicks={4} />
  )}
</Fit>
```

Both render in CSS pixels, so the tick labels are 11px whatever the width, and a `fontSize` on the chart is the one knob when the host's small text is another size. A figure given `width` alone takes its height from `aspect`; a figure given both ignores `aspect`. Without any of them a figure is 640 wide and shrinks, whole, inside a narrower host.

The chart text inherits the page font, so the `font-family` a recharts host set through a wrapper class is simply gone.

## Axes

A recharts axis draws itself and formats its own ticks. Here the value axis is opt-in and the category axis is a list of strings.

```
// recharts
<YAxis tickFormatter={fmtCompact} tickCount={4} />
<XAxis dataKey="date" ticks={pickTicks(rows, r => r.date)} tickFormatter={fmtDay} />

// diagrammatic
<Area yTicks={4} format={fmtCompact} labels={pickTicks(rows, 5).map(fmtDay)} />
```

`labels` are spread evenly across the plotted span, so pass as many as you want printed rather than one per point. The widest printed tick sizes the value gutter, so `YAxis width` has no counterpart. `yTicks` on log paper counts in decades; `decades()` helpers in the host can be deleted.

## Tooltips

The tooltip surface stays yours. What changes is where the values come from: the mark carries `data-i` and `data-series`, and the host reads its own row.

```
"use client";
import { Root, Tooltip } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

<Root>
  <Area series={series} labels={ticks} width={width} yTicks={4} />
  <Tooltip>
    {({ datum }) => {
      const row = rows[datum.index ?? 0];
      if (!row) return null;
      return (
        <div className="bg-popover ring-border rounded-lg px-2.5 py-2 shadow-md ring-1">
          <div className="font-mono text-xs">{fmtDay(row.date)}</div>
          {series.map((s) => (
            <Row key={s.name} label={s.name} value={format(row[s.name])} />
          ))}
        </div>
      );
    }}
  </Tooltip>
</Root>;
```

`datum.series` names the hovered series when the form has several, `datum.index2` addresses the second dimension of a grid, and `getSeriesColor(datum.element, name)` reads the rendered color for a swatch. A recharts `payload` mapper that formatted values inline becomes one lookup plus the formatting the host already owns.

Click and selection ride the same delegation: `onMarkClick` replaces a `Bar onClick`, and `highlight` replaces a selected-index style prop.

```
<Root
  onMarkClick={(datum) => router.push(rows[datum.index ?? 0].href)}
  highlight={selected == null ? null : { index: selected }}
>
```

## Color

A shadcn/ui host imports the shipped bridge once:

```
import "diagrammatic/shadcn.css";
```

It maps `--dg-c1` through `--dg-c5` to `--chart-1` through `--chart-5`, ink to `--foreground`, muted to `--muted-foreground`, grid to `--border`, and surface to `--background`. Any other system writes the same lines:

```
[data-dg],
[data-dg-legend] {
  --dg-c1: var(--chart-1);
  --dg-c2: var(--chart-2);
  --dg-c3: var(--chart-3);
  --dg-c4: var(--chart-4);
  --dg-c5: var(--chart-5);
  --dg-grid: var(--color-border);
  --dg-muted: var(--color-muted-foreground);
}
```

A `<Cell fill={chartColor(i)} />` per datum disappears: color follows the series or the category (`points[].series` on a scatter, `categorical` on a bar) and comes from the palette. The palette is seven categories; a host with an eighth ranks and folds the tail into `Other`. The `ChartConfig` that shadcn's wrapper needs to name and color each key becomes nothing: names come from the data and colors from the tokens.

## Legends

A recharts `Legend` is HTML positioned over the plot. Here the built-in legend is drawn inside the figure, and the DOM `Legend` is the counterpart on the page's own type:

```
import { Area, Legend } from "diagrammatic";

<Area series={series} legend={false} width={width} />
<Legend names={series.map((s) => s.name)} className="mt-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground" />
```

It is a plain list, server-safe, colored through the same tokens as the marks.

## Maps

`react-simple-maps` plus a `world-atlas` fetch plus a country-name table becomes `WorldMap` from `diagrammatic/world`, which carries Natural Earth 110m outlines as static path data and addresses countries by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Pan and zoom, which `ZoomableGroup` provided, is `Zoom` from `diagrammatic/interactive`.

```
<Root>
  <Zoom max={8}>
    {(view) => (
      <WorldMap
        values={{ US: 412, DE: 96, JP: 74 }}
        view={view}
        title="Sign-ins by country"
      />
    )}
  </Zoom>
  <Tooltip>{({ datum }) => <CountryTip iso={datum.series} />}</Tooltip>
</Root>
```

The function child is what keeps borders and country labels at their drawn weight while the map magnifies; a node child would scale them with the picture.

The name-to-ISO mapping is the host's migration, once, on the data rather than on every render.

## What does not come across

- Dual value axes. Two units on one frame is two figures.
- A `fill` per datum. Category color comes from `series` or `categorical`; an arbitrary color per row stays out, and a token override is how a host recolors.
- Animation props. The charts render once, on the server.
- A wrapper class that restyles chart internals (`[&_.recharts-cartesian-axis-tick_text]:fill-muted-foreground`). The tokens are the surface, and the type is already on the page's scale.

# Interaction
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/interaction

Tooltips, hover and controlled highlight, clicks, and the mark address every chart stamps.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Charts stay server components. Interaction lives in `diagrammatic/interactive`, a client entry whose components wrap a chart and read the addresses it stamps on its marks. A tooltip or a click handler receives an address, never the data: you look the row up in the data you already have.

\[interactive preview omitted]

## The mark address

Every drawn mark carries `data-part="mark"` and up to four address slots. Each form fills the slots its marks have (a parallel-coordinates record has a series but no index), and no form adds a fifth, so the interaction API never grows per form.

| Slot      | Attribute      | Meaning                                                       |
| --------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `index`   | `data-i`       | The primary ordinal: the point, bar, or category              |
| `index2`  | `data-i2`      | The secondary ordinal: the row of a grid                      |
| `series`  | `data-series`  | The identity: a series, a node, a country, or a flow's source |
| `series2` | `data-series2` | The counterparty: a flow's or an edge's target                |

`getMarkDatum(element)` decodes an element into that address, plus the `element` itself. It is what `Root` uses, and it works on its own in any event handler you attach to the chart's root.

## Root

`Root` is a `div` that delegates pointer events to the marks inside it.

| Prop               | Description                                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onMarkHover`      | Called with the datum when the pointer enters a mark, and with `null` when it leaves                    |
| `onMarkClick`      | Called with the datum and the event on a mark click                                                     |
| `highlightOnHover` | `true`, `"index"`, or `"series"`: what the hovered mark highlights. `true` tries `index`, then `series` |
| `highlight`        | A controlled `MarkQuery` or list of queries; while set, it wins over hover                              |

A highlight stamps `data-dg-active` on matching marks and `data-dg-muted` on the rest. `diagrammatic/styles.css` fades muted marks; restyle either state with your own CSS. `applyHighlight(container, query)` is the same stamp as a pure function, for a host driving it without `Root`.

```
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Line, type Series } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

export function TrafficChart({ series, weeks }: { series: Series[]; weeks: string[] }) {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <Root
      {...(selected && { highlight: { series: selected } })}
      highlightOnHover="series"
      onMarkClick={(datum) => setSelected(datum.series ?? null)}
    >
      <Line series={series} labels={weeks} />
    </Root>
  );
}
```

## Tooltip

`Tooltip` renders inside `Root` and follows the pointer over the hovered mark. Its child is a render function that receives the datum.

| Prop         | Description                                                                  | Default |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `side`       | `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, or `"right"`                                  | `"top"` |
| `sideOffset` | Distance from the pointer in pixels                                          | `10`    |
| `collision`  | Flip to the other side and clamp inside the container when it would overflow | `true`  |

Give the tooltip surface `width: max-content` (`w-max` in Tailwind), because an absolutely positioned box shrinks against its container's right edge and would change width as the pointer moves.

\[interactive preview omitted]

`getSeriesColor(element, series)` returns the color a series is drawn in, read from the live figure, so a tooltip swatch matches the chart under any theme.

## Without the wrapper

Every native SVG attribute and event handler passes through to a chart's root element, and refs forward. CSS alone can do hover emphasis:

```
svg[data-dg]:has([data-part="mark"]:hover) [data-part="mark"]:not(:hover) {
  opacity: 0.35;
}
```

## Accessibility

Marks are pointer affordances. The accessible path to the numbers is the chart's `title` and `summary` plus a table you render beside it; see [Accessibility](/diagrammatic/docs/accessibility).

# Motion
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/motion

Animate flow direction and live points with one attribute and the shipped stylesheet, on charts that stay server components.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Charts that draw a direction or a live reading stamp motion layers into their SVG. The layers are invisible and inert until two things are true: `diagrammatic/styles.css` is loaded, and the chart or any ancestor carries `data-dg-motion`. Motion is CSS only, so the chart stays a server component and no JavaScript runs to animate it.

```
import "diagrammatic/styles.css";
import { Sankey } from "diagrammatic";

<div data-dg-motion="">
  <Sankey graph={graph} />
</div>;
```

```tsx
import { Sankey } from "diagrammatic";

export default function SignupFlowSankey() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <Sankey
        title="Where this week's signups came from and went"
        labels={["source", "first action", "outcome"]}
        graph={{
          nodes: [
            { id: "search", group: 0 },
            { id: "docs", group: 0 },
            { id: "referral", group: 0 },
            { id: "template", group: 1 },
            { id: "blank", group: 1 },
            { id: "activated", group: 2 },
            { id: "dropped", group: 2 },
          ],
          links: [
            { source: "search", target: "template", value: 420 },
            { source: "search", target: "blank", value: 180 },
            { source: "docs", target: "template", value: 260 },
            { source: "docs", target: "blank", value: 140 },
            { source: "referral", target: "template", value: 120 },
            { source: "template", target: "activated", value: 610 },
            { source: "template", target: "dropped", value: 190 },
            { source: "blank", target: "activated", value: 110 },
            { source: "blank", target: "dropped", value: 210 },
          ],
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## What moves

| Layer      | Attribute                         | Charts                                                | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Flow trail | `data-dg-flow`                    | `Sankey`, `Chord`, `Network`, `ArcDiagram`, `FlowMap` | A comet travels each connection from its source to its target. In a `Sankey` one sweep crosses the columns in order: every ribbon in the first stage runs together, then hands off to the next stage |
| Flow step  | `data-dg-flow-step` with `--dg-t` | `DotWorldMap`                                         | The symbols along each trail light up in order, source first                                                                                                                                         |
| Pulse      | `data-dg-pulse`                   | `Line` with one series, `Sparkline`                   | A halo pulses from the latest point, for a live reading                                                                                                                                              |

Motion only explains something the still figure cannot: which way a connection runs, or that a value is live. Charts without either stay still.

```tsx
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function LiveTrafficMap() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <DotWorldMap
        title="Traffic failing over between regions, live"
        groups={{
          "us-east": ["US", "CA", "MX", "BR"],
          "eu-west": ["GB", "FR", "DE", "ES", "IT"],
          "ap-south": ["IN", "SG", "JP", "AU"],
        }}
        flows={[
          { from: "BR", to: "US" },
          { from: "GB", to: "US" },
          { from: "IN", to: "DE" },
          { from: "AU", to: "SG" },
          { from: "JP", to: "US" },
          { from: "DE", to: "SG" },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Live readings

Toggle the attribute with the data source, so the pulse means the reading is live.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

const WINDOW = 30;
const REDUCED = "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)";

function subscribe(onChange: () => void) {
  const query = window.matchMedia(REDUCED);
  query.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  return () => query.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
}

function next(prev: number[], t: number): number[] {
  const last = prev[prev.length - 1] ?? 40;
  const noise = Math.abs(Math.sin(t * 12.9898) * 43758.5453) % 1;
  const drift = Math.sin(t / 6) * 3 + noise * 4 - 2;
  return [...prev.slice(1), Math.max(5, Math.min(95, last + drift))];
}

export default function LiveCpuChart() {
  const [data, setData] = useState(() =>
    Array.from({ length: WINDOW }, (_, i) => 40 + Math.sin(i / 4) * 8),
  );
  const reduced = useSyncExternalStore(
    subscribe,
    () => window.matchMedia(REDUCED).matches,
    () => false,
  );
  const [choice, setChoice] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
  const running = choice ?? !reduced;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!running) return;
    let t = 0;
    const id = setInterval(() => {
      t += 1;
      setData((prev) => next(prev, t));
    }, 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [running]);

  return (
    <div data-dg-motion={running ? "" : undefined}>
      <Line
        title="CPU, last 30 seconds"
        data={data}
        yMax={100}
        yTicks={[
          { at: 0, label: "0%" },
          { at: 50, label: "50%" },
          { at: 100, label: "100%" },
        ]}
        format={(v) => `${Math.round(v)}%`}
      />
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={() => setChoice(!running)}
        className="text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground mt-3 text-xs"
      >
        {running ? "Pause" : "Resume"}
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Reduced motion

Every motion rule sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. A reader who asks for reduced motion sees the still figure, with nothing for you to check.

## Timing and style

`--dg-motion-duration` sets how long one pass takes (2.4s by default). Every trail in a figure shares that one pass; each trail carries `--dg-flow-from` and `--dg-flow-to`, the offsets that place its comet in the sweep, so leave its dash pattern to the stylesheet and restyle color, width, or opacity instead.

```
[data-dg-motion] {
  --dg-motion-duration: 4s;
}
[data-dg-motion] [data-dg-flow] {
  stroke-opacity: 0.6;
}
```

A highlighted chart hides the trails of muted connections and keeps them in step with the sweep, so a highlight reads the same in motion as at rest.

## Without the stylesheet

The layers draw nothing on their own: a trail has `stroke-opacity="0"` and a pulse has `opacity="0"`. A host that skips `styles.css` can write its own keyframes against the same attributes, or leave the charts still.

# Zoom
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/zoom

Pan and scale a figure that holds more detail than its frame.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

`Zoom` from `diagrammatic/interactive` pans and scales a figure. The wheel scales about the pointer, a drag pans, and a double click or `Escape` resets. The transform lives on the wrapper, so the chart inside stays a server component and is not redrawn by the wrapper itself.

\[interactive preview omitted]

## Two modes

The child decides how the figure zooms.

- **A node** is scaled as rendered. Stroke widths and type scale with it, which is what arbitrary content needs.
- **A function** receives the `view` window and hands it to a chart, which redraws through it. Hairlines and labels keep their drawn size at any magnification, which is what a map wants.

```
"use client";

import { Zoom } from "diagrammatic/interactive";
import { WorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

<Zoom max={8}>{(view) => <WorldMap values={byCountry} view={view} />}</Zoom>;
```

`view` is a window in fractions of the box: `{ x: 0, y: 0, w: 1, h: 1 }` is the whole figure, and `w: 0.5` is twice the magnification. Fractions rather than pixels mean the same window at any `width`.

## Props

| Prop               | Description                              | Default    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `min` / `max`      | The scale range                          | `1` / `12` |
| `transform`        | A controlled `{ k, x, y }` transform     |            |
| `defaultTransform` | The starting transform when uncontrolled | Identity   |
| `onChange`         | Called with each new transform           |            |
| `disabled`         | Turns pan and zoom off                   | `false`    |

`viewOf`, `zoomAbout`, and `IDENTITY` are exported for a host that drives its own transform, such as zoom buttons or a minimap. Nest `Zoom` inside `Root` to keep tooltips and highlight working through the transform.

## Motion

Each arc carries a trail from its `source` to its `target`, whichever side of the axis the source sits on. Put `data-dg-motion` on the chart or any ancestor; see [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
import { ArcDiagram } from "diagrammatic";

export default function ImportArcs() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <ArcDiagram
        aspect={2.2}
        title="Which modules import which, in file order"
        graph={{
          nodes: ["cli", "cfg", "core", "db", "api", "net", "ui", "log"].map(
            (id) => ({ id }),
          ),
          links: [
            { source: "cli", target: "cfg" },
            { source: "cli", target: "ui" },
            { source: "core", target: "db" },
            { source: "core", target: "log" },
            { source: "api", target: "db" },
            { source: "api", target: "net" },
            { source: "ui", target: "log" },
            { source: "log", target: "cfg" },

    </div>
  );
}
```

Illustrative data. Incident handoffs, Q2 2025. n = 147.

fig. 47 · On-call handoffs, one quarter

Payments into checkout is the thickest ribbon at 38, and the return carries 22. Growth sends 18 into checkout and seven into search. Platform sends 27 across payments and search and receives eight from payments.

- Use it for

  Dense mutual exchange: migration, trade, traffic between equals.

- Watch out

  Beautiful and hard to read; reserve it for genuinely circular relationships.

## Motion

Each ribbon carries a trail from the group it leaves to the group it reaches, which a chord cannot show at rest. Put `data-dg-motion` on the chart or any ancestor; see [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
import { Chord } from "diagrammatic";

export default function HandoffChord() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <Chord
        aspect={1.15}
        title="On-call handoffs between teams"
        groups={["payments", "checkout", "search", "growth", "platform"]}
        flows={[
          { from: "payments", to: "checkout", value: 38 },
          { from: "checkout", to: "payments", value: 22 },
          { from: "checkout", to: "search", value: 14 },
          { from: "growth", to: "checkout", value: 18 },
          { from: "platform", to: "payments", value: 16 },
          { from: "platform", to: "search", value: 11 },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

- yLabel

  hours to first review

Illustrative data. First-review hours against files changed. n = 300.

fig. 37 · Review hours against files changed

Most reviews are small diffs answered within a few hours. A smaller group of large diffs takes most of a working day. Bigger diffs wait longer, and the rings say by how much.

- Use it for

  The shape of a dense 2D distribution without overplotting.

- Watch out

  Levels are model output; annotate what each band means.

Illustrative data. Ticket topic merge distances.

fig. 52 · Support ticket topic merges

Login, 2fa, and session join first. Billing, refund, and invoice join next. The auth and billing clusters join at 0.40. Export, api-key, and webhook form another cluster by 0.28. Other hangs off the last join at 0.78.

- Use it for

- Watch out

  Height is the metric; cutting at a level is what defines the clusters.

# Dot world map
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/charts/dot-world-map

The world as a halftone field of dots. Countries color by named group, and flows draw as trails between countries.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Legend } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root, Tooltip } from "diagrammatic/interactive";
import { DotWorldMap, WORLD } from "diagrammatic/world";

const NAMES = new Map(WORLD.map((country) => [country.iso, country.name]));
const REGIONS = {
  "us-east": ["US", "CA", "MX", "BR", "AR", "CO", "CL"],
  "eu-west": ["GB", "IE", "FR", "DE", "NL", "ES", "IT", "PL", "SE", "NO"],
  "ap-south": ["IN", "SG", "ID", "AU", "JP", "KR", "TH", "VN"],
};
const REGION_OF = new Map(
  Object.entries(REGIONS).flatMap(([region, list]) =>
    list.map((iso) => [iso, region]),
  ),
);

export default function InferenceRegionsMap() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <Legend names={Object.keys(REGIONS)} className="mb-3 text-xs" />
      <Root highlightOnHover="series">
        <DotWorldMap
          title="Inference regions and the countries they serve"
          groups={REGIONS}
          flows={[
            { from: "BR", to: "US" },
            { from: "GB", to: "US" },
            { from: "IN", to: "DE" },
            { from: "AU", to: "SG" },
            { from: "JP", to: "US" },
            { from: "DE", to: "SG" },
          ]}
        />
        <Tooltip side="top">
          {({ datum }) => {
            if (!datum.series) return null;
            const text = datum.series2
              ? `${NAMES.get(datum.series)} to ${NAMES.get(datum.series2)}`
              : `${NAMES.get(datum.series) ?? datum.series}, ${REGION_OF.get(datum.series) ?? "not served"}`;
            return (
              <div className="bg-popover text-popover-foreground w-max rounded-lg border px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs shadow-md">
                {text}
              </div>
            );
          }}
        </Tooltip>
      </Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Usage

```
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

<DotWorldMap
  groups={{ "us-east": ["US", "CA"], "eu-west": ["GB", "DE"] }}
  flows={[{ from: "US", to: "GB" }]}
/>;
```

Use it when the question is where, not how much: a footprint, a coverage map, a replication topology. For a value per country, use the [World map](/diagrammatic/docs/charts/world-map).

## Examples

### A footprint

One group lights up a set of countries; every other country stays a faint dot.

```tsx
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function FootprintMap() {
  return (
    <DotWorldMap
      title="Where we ship"
      groups={{ shipping: ["US", "CA", "GB", "DE", "FR", "JP", "AU"] }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Groups

`groups` maps a name to a list of country codes. Groups take the categorical palette in their key order. The map draws no legend of its own; put the DOM `Legend` above it with the same names, as the figure at the top does.

```tsx
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function TimezoneTeamsMap() {
  return (
    <DotWorldMap
      title="Support coverage by team"
      groups={{
        Americas: ["US", "CA", "MX", "BR", "AR", "CO", "CL", "PE"],
        EMEA: [
          "GB",
          "IE",
          "FR",
          "DE",
          "ES",
          "IT",
          "NL",
          "SE",
          "PL",
          "ZA",
          "NG",
          "EG",
          "AE",
          "SA",
        ],
        APAC: ["IN", "CN", "JP", "KR", "SG", "ID", "AU", "NZ", "PH", "VN"],
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Flows

`flows` draws a lifted trail from one country to another, blending from the source group's color to the target's.

```tsx
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function ReplicationMap() {
  return (
    <DotWorldMap
      title="Database replication from the primary in Virginia"
      groups={{
        primary: ["US"],
        replicas: ["GB", "DE", "JP", "SG", "BR", "AU"],
      }}
      flows={["GB", "DE", "JP", "SG", "BR", "AU"].map((to) => ({
        from: "US",
        to,
      }))}
    />
  );
}
```

### Animated flows

Put `data-dg-motion` on the map or any ancestor and each trail runs from source to target, so the direction reads without arrows. See [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function LiveTrafficMap() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <DotWorldMap
        title="Traffic failing over between regions, live"
        groups={{
          "us-east": ["US", "CA", "MX", "BR"],
          "eu-west": ["GB", "FR", "DE", "ES", "IT"],
          "ap-south": ["IN", "SG", "JP", "AU"],
        }}
        flows={[
          { from: "BR", to: "US" },
          { from: "GB", to: "US" },
          { from: "IN", to: "DE" },
          { from: "AU", to: "SG" },
          { from: "JP", to: "US" },
          { from: "DE", to: "SG" },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Interaction

Each country is a mark with `data-series` set to its code, and each flow carries its source in `series` and its target in `series2`, so one tooltip can describe both, as the figure at the top does.

### Zoom

```tsx
"use client";

import { Zoom } from "diagrammatic/interactive";
import { DotWorldMap } from "diagrammatic/world";

export default function ZoomableDotMap() {
  return (
    <Zoom max={6} className="overflow-hidden rounded-md">
      {(view) => (
        <DotWorldMap
          title="Edge locations in Europe"
          groups={{
            edge: [
              "GB",
              "IE",
              "FR",
              "DE",
              "NL",
              "ES",
              "IT",
              "SE",
              "PL",
              "CH",
              "AT",
            ],
          }}
          view={view}
        />
      )}
    </Zoom>
  );
}
```

## Props

- `groups?`: `Record<string, string[]>` — Named sets of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, colored in key order.
- `flows?`: `{ from: string; to: string }[]` — Trails between two countries, by code.
- `title?`: `string` — Names the map for assistive technology.
- `summary?`: `string` — A sentence read after the title.
- `width`: `number` (default `640`) — Rendered width in CSS pixels.
- `height?`: `number` — Rendered height in CSS pixels.
- `aspect?`: `number` — Width over height when \`height\` is not given.
- `view?`: `{ x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }` — A window onto the map, from \`Zoom\`.

## Motion

```tsx
import { FlowMap } from "diagrammatic";

export default function EgressFlowMap() {

      <FlowMap
        aspect={1.7}
        title="Egress from iad-1, live"
        origin={{ col: 13, row: 2, label: "iad-1" }}
        routes={[
          { col: 4, row: 1, value: 84 },
          { col: 14, row: 3, value: 41 },
          { col: 15, row: 3, value: 28 },
          { col: 11, row: 6, value: 19 },
          { col: 5, row: 6, value: 12 },

  It shows plan, not progress; pair the bars with a done state or a today line.

# All charts
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/charts

Every chart form, grouped by the question it answers. Open one for its examples and props.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

Every form has a page here except `Pictogram`, `RadialBar`, and `StripPlot`, which ship in the package and the spec. The data in every example is illustrative.

### [Change over time](/diagrammatic/docs/charts#change-over-time)

Trends, rhythms, and histories. The x axis is time; everything else is a choice.

# Line
URL: /diagrammatic/docs/charts/line

The default for anything measured over time. One series or several, on linear or log paper, with regions, bands, annotations, and guides.

> For AI agents: a documentation index is available at [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Use `.md` for canonical markdown pages; `.mdx` is kept as a backwards-compatible alias on supported URL paths.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Line } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root, Tooltip, getSeriesColor } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

const STEPS = Array.from({ length: 16 }, (_, i) => (i === 0 ? "0" : `${i}k`));
const SERIES = [
  {
    name: "baseline",
    data: [
      220, 244, 271, 301, 334, 369, 405, 441, 476, 509, 539, 566, 589, 608, 622,
      631,
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "fixed penalty",
    data: [
      220, 238, 252, 248, 225, 201, 182, 169, 161, 156, 153, 151, 150, 150, 149,
      149,
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "alternating",
    data: [
      220, 248, 282, 320, 352, 344, 310, 285, 272, 266, 269, 273, 272, 274, 273,
      275,
    ],
  },
];

export default function ResponseLengthChart() {
  return (
    <Root highlightOnHover="series">
      <Line
        title="Mean response length by training recipe"
        summary="Baseline grows to 631 tokens, the fixed penalty falls to 149, and only the alternating recipe settles in the 250 to 300 band."
        aspect={2.2}
        series={SERIES}
        labels={STEPS.map((step, i) => (i % 2 === 0 ? step : ""))}
        yTicks={[
          { at: 200, label: "200" },
          { at: 400, label: "400" },
          { at: 600, label: "600" },
        ]}
        bands={[{ lower: STEPS.map(() => 250), upper: STEPS.map(() => 300) }]}
        regions={[{ from: 4, to: 9, label: "alternating penalty" }]}
        guides={[{ at: 275, label: "target 275" }]}
        marks={[
          { series: "alternating", at: 4, label: "penalty on" },
          { series: "alternating", at: 9, label: "off" },
          { series: "baseline", at: 15, label: "631" },
          { series: "fixed penalty", at: 15, label: "149" },
        ]}
      />
      <Tooltip side="top">
        {({ datum }) => {
          const i = datum.index;
          if (i === undefined) return null;
          return (
            <div className="bg-popover text-popover-foreground w-max rounded-lg border px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs shadow-md">
              <div className="text-muted-foreground mb-1">step {STEPS[i]}</div>
              {SERIES.map((s) => (
                <div key={s.name} className="flex items-center gap-2">
                  <span
                    className="size-2 rounded-full"
                    style={{
                      background: getSeriesColor(datum.element, s.name),
                    }}
                  />
                  <span className="flex-1">{s.name}</span>
                  <span className="tabular-nums">{s.data[i]}</span>
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>
          );
        }}
      </Tooltip>
    </Root>
  );
}
```

## Usage

```
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

<Line labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"]} data={[34, 46, 40]} />;
```

`Line` renders on the server. Pass `data` for one series or `series` for several; `labels` names the points on the x axis.

## Examples

### One series

A single series draws in ink with its last value printed at the end of the line.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function ActiveUsersChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="Monthly active users"
      labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep"]}
      data={[34, 46, 40, 58, 52, 66, 60, 76, 90]}
      format={(v) => `${v}k`}
    />
  );
}
```

### Several series

Two or more named series take the categorical palette in order and get a legend. Past four lines, consider [small multiples](/diagrammatic/docs/small-multiples).

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function LatencyByRegionChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="p95 latency by region, ms"
      labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
      series={[
        { name: "us-east", data: [182, 176, 191, 204, 188, 160, 152] },
        { name: "eu-west", data: [214, 220, 209, 231, 246, 198, 190] },
        { name: "ap-south", data: [268, 281, 274, 259, 262, 240, 236] },
      ]}
      yTicks={4}
    />
  );
}
```

### Steps

`step` holds each value until the next one, for quantities that change in discrete jumps: seats, prices, replica counts.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function SeatCountChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      step
      title="Paid seats"
      labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6", "W7", "W8", "W9", "W10"]}
      data={[40, 40, 55, 55, 55, 80, 80, 80, 120, 120]}
      yTicks={4}
    />
  );
}
```

### Regions and annotations

`regions` shades a span of the x axis in index units, and `marks` pins a label to a point. Together they tell the reader why the line moved.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

const HOURS = Array.from(
  { length: 13 },
  (_, i) => `${String(i * 2).padStart(2, "0")}:00`,
);

export default function ErrorRateChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="Checkout error rate, %"
      labels={HOURS.map((h, i) => (i % 2 === 0 ? h : ""))}
      data={[0.4, 0.5, 0.4, 0.6, 2.8, 3.4, 1.1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.4, 0.5, 0.4, 0.4]}
      regions={[{ from: 3.5, to: 6, label: "incident" }]}
      marks={[
        { at: 4, label: "deploy 4812" },
        { at: 6, label: "rollback" },
      ]}
      yTicks={3}
    />
  );
}
```

### Uncertainty bands

`bands` takes a `lower` and `upper` array per series and draws the range under the line, for forecasts and confidence intervals.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

const MONTHS = [
  "Jan",
  "Feb",
  "Mar",
  "Apr",
  "May",
  "Jun",
  "Jul",
  "Aug",
  "Sep",
  "Oct",
  "Nov",
  "Dec",
];
const FORECAST = [120, 128, 134, 141, 150, 158, 163, 171, 180, 188, 195, 204];

export default function DemandForecastChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="GPU hours forecast, thousands"
      labels={MONTHS}
      series={[{ name: "forecast", data: FORECAST }]}
      bands={[
        {
          lower: FORECAST.map((v, i) => v - 4 - i * 2.2),
          upper: FORECAST.map((v, i) => v + 4 + i * 2.2),
        },
      ]}
      yTicks={4}
    />
  );
}
```

### Thresholds

`guides` draws reference lines on either axis: an SLO on the value axis, a deploy on the x axis.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

const HOURS = Array.from(
  { length: 12 },
  (_, i) => `${String(i * 2).padStart(2, "0")}:00`,
);

export default function SloChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="p95 latency, ms"
      labels={HOURS}
      data={[212, 220, 231, 226, 240, 238, 251, 296, 318, 284, 262, 248]}
      yTicks={4}
      guides={[
        { at: 300, label: "SLO" },
        { at: 7, axis: "x", label: "deploy" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Log scale

`yScale="log"` puts growth that spans decades on one frame. A tick count on log paper counts decades.

```tsx
import { Line, formatCompact } from "diagrammatic";

export default function StarsChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="Cumulative GitHub stars"
      labels={[
        "M1",
        "M2",
        "M3",
        "M4",
        "M5",
        "M6",
        "M7",
        "M8",
        "M9",
        "M10",
        "M11",
        "M12",
      ]}
      data={[
        180, 420, 760, 1500, 2600, 4100, 6900, 9800, 14200, 21500, 30100, 41800,
      ]}
      yScale="log"
      yTicks={3}
      format={formatCompact}
    />
  );
}
```

### Uneven x positions

`xs` places points at numeric x positions instead of evenly, and `xScale="log"` spaces them logarithmically, as a scaling curve needs.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function EvalLossChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      title="Validation loss against training tokens, billions"
      xs={[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]}
      xScale="log"
      xTicks={[
        { at: 1, label: "1B" },
        { at: 8, label: "8B" },
        { at: 64, label: "64B" },
      ]}
      series={[
        { name: "350M", data: [3.9, 3.6, 3.35, 3.16, 3.02, 2.93, 2.88, 2.86] },
        { name: "1.3B", data: [3.8, 3.42, 3.11, 2.86, 2.68, 2.55, 2.47, 2.42] },
      ]}
      yTicks={3}
      format={(v) => v.toFixed(1)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Survival curves

A `step` line with `marks` of `kind: "censor"` is a Kaplan-Meier plot: the ticks mark where observation stopped without an event.

```tsx
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

export default function RetentionChart() {
  return (
    <Line
      step
      title="Share of trial workspaces still active"
      labels={["0", "", "", "30d", "", "", "60d", "", "", "90d"]}
      series={[
        {
          name: "with onboarding",
          data: [1, 0.94, 0.9, 0.86, 0.84, 0.82, 0.81, 0.8, 0.79, 0.79],
        },
        {
          name: "without",
          data: [1, 0.88, 0.79, 0.71, 0.66, 0.62, 0.6, 0.57, 0.55, 0.54],
        },
      ]}
      marks={[
        { series: "with onboarding", at: 4, kind: "censor" },
        { series: "with onboarding", at: 7, kind: "censor" },
        { series: "without", at: 5, kind: "censor" },
      ]}
      yTicks={[
        { at: 0.5, label: "50%" },
        { at: 0.75, label: "75%" },
        { at: 1, label: "100%" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Interaction

These examples wrap the server-rendered chart in `diagrammatic/interactive`. See [Interaction](/diagrammatic/docs/interaction) for the full API.

### Tooltip

The tooltip receives the hovered point's `index` and looks the value up in your data.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Line } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root, Tooltip } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

const DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"];
const REQUESTS = [12.4, 13.1, 12.8, 14.6, 15.2, 9.8, 8.9];

export default function RequestsChart() {
  return (
    <Root>
      <Line
        title="Requests per second, thousands"
        labels={DAYS}
        data={REQUESTS}
        yTicks={3}
      />
      <Tooltip side="top">
        {({ datum }) => {
          const i = datum.index;
          if (i === undefined) return null;
          return (
            <div className="bg-popover text-popover-foreground w-max rounded-lg border px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs shadow-md">
              <span className="text-muted-foreground">{DAYS[i]}</span>{" "}
              <span className="font-medium tabular-nums">
                {REQUESTS[i]}k rps
              </span>
            </div>
          );
        }}
      </Tooltip>
    </Root>
  );
}
```

### Highlight a series

A controlled `highlight` fades every other series; `highlightOnHover="series"` does the same while the pointer rests on a line.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

const SERIES = [
  { name: "search", data: [42, 48, 51, 58, 61, 66, 64, 71, 77, 82] },
  { name: "direct", data: [30, 29, 33, 35, 34, 38, 41, 40, 43, 45] },
  { name: "referral", data: [12, 15, 14, 18, 22, 21, 25, 29, 28, 33] },
  { name: "social", data: [8, 9, 13, 12, 11, 15, 14, 18, 21, 19] },
];

export default function ChannelChart() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div>
      <div className="mb-3 flex flex-wrap gap-1.5">
        {SERIES.map((s) => (
          <button
            key={s.name}
            type="button"
            aria-pressed={selected === s.name}
            onClick={() => setSelected(selected === s.name ? null : s.name)}
            className="aria-pressed:bg-foreground aria-pressed:text-background rounded-md border px-2 py-1 text-xs"
          >
            {s.name}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <Root
        {...(selected && { highlight: { series: selected } })}
        highlightOnHover="series"
      >
        <Line
          title="Weekly sessions by channel, thousands"
          labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6", "W7", "W8", "W9", "W10"]}
          series={SERIES}
          yTicks={4}
        />
      </Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Select a point

`onMarkClick` reports the clicked point's address, and a controlled highlight keeps the selection visible.

```tsx
"use client";

import { useState } from "react";
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";
import { Root, type MarkDatum } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

const BUILDS = [
  "#4801",
  "#4802",
  "#4803",
  "#4804",
  "#4805",
  "#4806",
  "#4807",
  "#4808",
];
const DURATION = [6.2, 6.4, 6.1, 9.8, 6.3, 6.0, 6.6, 6.2];
const CAUSE = [
  "",
  "",
  "",
  "cold cache after the runner image bump",
  "",
  "",
  "",
  "",
];

export default function BuildTimeChart() {
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState<number>(3);

  return (
    <div>
      <Root
        highlight={{ index: picked }}
        onMarkClick={(datum: MarkDatum) => {
          if (datum.index !== undefined) setPicked(datum.index);
        }}
      >
        <Line
          title="CI duration, minutes"
          labels={BUILDS}
          data={DURATION}
          yTicks={3}
        />
      </Root>
      <p className="text-muted-foreground mt-3 text-sm">
        <span className="text-foreground font-medium">{BUILDS[picked]}</span>{" "}
        took <span className="tabular-nums">{DURATION[picked]} min</span>
        {CAUSE[picked] ? `: ${CAUSE[picked]}.` : "."} Click a point to inspect
        another build.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Live data

The chart is a pure function of its props, so streaming data is a state update. This one appends a reading every second, and `data-dg-motion` pulses the latest point while it runs. See [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { Line } from "diagrammatic";

const WINDOW = 30;
const REDUCED = "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)";

function subscribe(onChange: () => void) {
  const query = window.matchMedia(REDUCED);
  query.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  return () => query.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
}

function next(prev: number[], t: number): number[] {
  const last = prev[prev.length - 1] ?? 40;
  const noise = Math.abs(Math.sin(t * 12.9898) * 43758.5453) % 1;
  const drift = Math.sin(t / 6) * 3 + noise * 4 - 2;
  return [...prev.slice(1), Math.max(5, Math.min(95, last + drift))];
}

export default function LiveCpuChart() {
  const [data, setData] = useState(() =>
    Array.from({ length: WINDOW }, (_, i) => 40 + Math.sin(i / 4) * 8),
  );
  const reduced = useSyncExternalStore(
    subscribe,
    () => window.matchMedia(REDUCED).matches,
    () => false,
  );
  const [choice, setChoice] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
  const running = choice ?? !reduced;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!running) return;
    let t = 0;
    const id = setInterval(() => {
      t += 1;
      setData((prev) => next(prev, t));
    }, 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, [running]);

  return (
    <div data-dg-motion={running ? "" : undefined}>
      <Line
        title="CPU, last 30 seconds"
        data={data}
        yMax={100}
        yTicks={[
          { at: 0, label: "0%" },
          { at: 50, label: "50%" },
          { at: 100, label: "100%" },
        ]}
        format={(v) => `${Math.round(v)}%`}
      />
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={() => setChoice(!running)}
        className="text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground mt-3 text-xs"
      >
        {running ? "Pause" : "Resume"}
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Fluid width

`Fit` measures its box and hands the width down, so the frame is laid out again at every width and the type stays at 11px. Resize the window.

```tsx
"use client";

import { Line } from "diagrammatic";
import { Fit } from "diagrammatic/interactive";

export default function FluidChart() {
  return (
    <Fit>
      {({ width }) => (
        <Line
          title="Daily signups"
          width={width}
          aspect={3}
          labels={[
            "1",
            "",
            "",
            "",
            "5",
            "",
            "",
            "",
            "",
            "10",
            "",
            "",
            "",
            "",
            "15",
          ]}
          data={[12, 14, 13, 17, 21, 19, 24, 28, 27, 33, 31, 36, 41, 39, 45]}
          yTicks={3}
        />
      )}
    </Fit>
  );
}
```

## From a spec

The same chart as JSON, for a model to write. See [Charts from a model](/diagrammatic/docs/ai-specs).

```tsx
import { Chart, validateSpec } from "diagrammatic/spec";

const modelOutput = `{
  "v": "dg/1",
  "type": "line",
  "title": "Weekly active users",
  "unit": "compact",
  "labels": ["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6"],
  "data": [1200, 1350, 1310, 1580, 1720, 1910],
  "yTicks": 3
}`;

export default function SpecChart() {
  return <Chart spec={validateSpec(JSON.parse(modelOutput))} />;
}
```

## When to use it

- **Use it for** trends, rates, and anything measured on a continuous timeline.
- **Watch out** for more than four lines, which turn to spaghetti; facet into small multiples instead. For a quantity that accumulates, an [area](/diagrammatic/docs/charts/area) reads better.

## Props

- `data?`: `number[]` — One series of values. Use \`series\` for several.
- `series?`: `{ name: string; data: number[] }[]` — Named series, colored in palette order. Two or more get a legend.
- `labels?`: `string[]` — One label per point on the x axis. An empty string skips a label.
- `xs?`: `number[]` — Numeric x positions, one per point, instead of even spacing.
- `xScale`: `"linear" | "log"` (default `"linear"`) — The x scale when \`xs\` is given.
- `yScale`: `"linear" | "log"` (default `"linear"`) — The value scale.
- `yMax?`: `number` — Fixes the top of the value axis, so several charts share a scale.
- `xTicks?`: `number | { at: number; label: string }[]` — A tick count or an explicit ladder on the x axis.
- `yTicks?`: `number | { at: number; label: string }[]` — A tick count or an explicit ladder on the value axis. Unset draws no value axis.
- `step`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Holds each value until the next point.
- `regions?`: `{ from: number; to: number; label?: string }[]` — Shaded spans of the x axis, in index units or \`xs\` units.
- `bands?`: `{ lower: number[]; upper: number[] }[]` — A range under each series, in series order.
- `marks?`: `{ at: number; series?: string; label?: string; kind?: "point" | "censor" }[]` — Annotations pinned to points. \`kind: "censor"\` draws a censoring tick.
- `guides?`: `{ at: number; axis?: "x" | "y"; label?: string }[]` — Reference lines. The value axis by default.
- `legend?`: `boolean` — The in-figure legend. On when there are two or more series.
- `format`: `(value: number) => string` (default `formatCompact`) — Formats printed values and tick labels.
- `title?`: `string` — Names the chart for assistive technology. See [Accessibility](/diagrammatic/docs/accessibility).
- `summary?`: `string` — A sentence read after the title.
- `width`: `number` (default `640`) — Rendered width in CSS pixels. See [Sizing](/diagrammatic/docs/sizing).
- `height?`: `number` — Rendered height in CSS pixels. Defaults to \`width / aspect\`.
- `aspect?`: `number` — Width over height when \`height\` is not given.
- `fontSize`: `number` (default `11`) — The type size in CSS pixels.
- `view?`: `{ x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }` — A window onto the figure, from \`Zoom\`.

Every other SVG attribute, event handler, `style`, and `ref` passes through to the root `svg`.

Gateway connects to checkout, auth, cart, and flags. Checkout connects to payments, inventory, pricing, and risk. Risk is the only service linked to both checkout and payments.

- Use it for

  Structure in connections: hubs, bridges, and islands.

- Watch out

  Force layouts are unstable art; pin the nodes readers must find.

## Motion

Each link carries a trail from its `source` to its `target`, turning an undirected-looking graph into a call path. Put `data-dg-motion` on the chart or any ancestor; see [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
import { Network } from "diagrammatic";

export default function RequestPathNetwork() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <Network
        aspect={1.2}
        title="Calls made by one checkout request"
        graph={{
          nodes: [
            { id: "gw", label: "gateway" },
            { id: "checkout", label: "checkout" },
            { id: "pay", label: "payments" },
            { id: "inv", label: "inventory" },
            { id: "risk", label: "risk" },
            { id: "email", label: "email" },
          ],
          links: [
            { source: "gw", target: "checkout" },
            { source: "checkout", target: "pay" },
            { source: "checkout", target: "inv" },
            { source: "pay", target: "risk" },
            { source: "pay", target: "email" },
          ],
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Motion

One sweep crosses the columns in order: every ribbon in the first stage runs together, then hands off to the next, so the flow reads left to right without arrows. Put `data-dg-motion` on the chart or any ancestor; see [Motion](/diagrammatic/docs/motion).

```tsx
import { Sankey } from "diagrammatic";

export default function SignupFlowSankey() {
  return (
    <div data-dg-motion="">
      <Sankey
        title="Where this week's signups came from and went"
        labels={["source", "first action", "outcome"]}
        graph={{
          nodes: [
            { id: "search", group: 0 },
            { id: "docs", group: 0 },
            { id: "referral", group: 0 },
            { id: "template", group: 1 },
            { id: "blank", group: 1 },
            { id: "activated", group: 2 },
            { id: "dropped", group: 2 },
          ],
          links: [
            { source: "search", target: "template", value: 420 },
            { source: "search", target: "blank", value: 180 },
            { source: "docs", target: "template", value: 260 },
            { source: "docs", target: "blank", value: 140 },
            { source: "referral", target: "template", value: 120 },
            { source: "template", target: "activated", value: 610 },
            { source: "template", target: "dropped", value: 190 },
            { source: "blank", target: "activated", value: 110 },
            { source: "blank", target: "dropped", value: 210 },
          ],
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```
